LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Pete Prisco reveals all of his Week 8 picks, including the Bills to top the Ravens in a high-scoring game Imagn Images Going to the dogs last week turned out to be dog doodoo. I picked every dog against the spread last week and it looked good early, but then it collapsed late with five straight losses, including both prime-time games Sunday and Monday night. I was 8-6 straight up last week and 6-7-1 against the spread. Hey, the spread record was an improvement, which tells you how bad I've been this season. My ATS record this year is 43-61-3, which is a long way from .500. My straight-up record is 62-44-1. So this week, it's back to just picking the games. Forget all dogs. Trying to get to .500 makes me borrow a coaching cliché they all use. One game at a time. One week at a time. Turnaround time. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime These two are both coming off losses. The Carolina loss featured the Bucs running over them for 258 rushing yards. It's been a problem all year. But the Packers don't run it very well, so something has to give. Carolina gave Jordan Love fits last year, but that will change here. Carolina gives up 27.7 points per game. Love lights them up and Josh Jacobs gets the run game going. Pick: Packers 31, Panthers 24 Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Lamar Jackson could be back for the Ravens, but how much will his injured ankle impact his ability to move? The Bills are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. Baltimore's defense was bad in the loss to the Bengals last week, but Buffalo's defense has been awful. Look for a shootout here with Josh Allen getting the best of it. Pick: Bills 35, Ravens 30 Tennessee Titans at Cincinnati Bengals (-10.5) The Titans are having major problems on offense, while the Bengals lit up the Ravens last week. Joe Burrow was special in the second half of that game and I think that will carry over here. Look for an offensive explosion from the Bengals as Burrow starts to get into the MVP talk. Pick: Bengals 36, Titans 10 Arizona Cardinals at Dallas Cowboys (-6.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys' offense came alive against the Eagles Monday night, especially on the ground, which isn't a good thing for an Arizona defense that is last in the league in scoring. The Dallas offense should roll and the Arizona offense won't be able to keep up. Dallas big — even on a short week. Pick: Cowboys 37, Cardinals 21 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) The undefeated Vikings face a tough road game here against Detroit. The Lions offense against the Minnesota defense will be a treat to watch. Jared Goff is playing at a high level right now, but Minnesota's defense is the best in the league in terms of scoring. The Vikings offense is limited, but the Detroit defense has had major problems. But they were better last week, which I think carries over. Lions take it. Pick: Lions 23, Vikings 13 Las Vegas Raiders at New York Jets (-1.5) Kirk Cousins stays in as the starter for the Raiders, but teams have blitzed him the past two weeks. That could be a problem here since the Jets are a top-10 team in blitz percentage. The Raiders have struggled to stop opposing offenses, giving up 28.1 points per game, so look for Geno Smith to have success. Jets win it. Pick: Jets 27, Raiders 16 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) This is a big game for the division lead in the AFC North. The Browns beat the Steelers earlier this year, but this will be a bigger challenge on the road. They are also playing consecutive road games, which will be a challenge. Look for Aaron Rodgers to play well as the Steelers take it. Pick: Steelers 24, Browns 20 Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-2.5) This is suddenly a big game in the NFC South with the Bucs upsetting Carolina last week and the Falcons upsetting the 49ers. The Tampa Bay running game has come alive, but Atlanta is stingy on the ground, giving up 3.8 per rush. That will mean this is a Baker Mayfield game. Tampa Bay gives up 3.5 per rush, which might make for tough going for Bijan Robinson. That's a problem for the Atlanta offense. Tampa Bay wins it. Pick: Bucs 23, Falcons 17 Indianapolis Colts at Jacksonville Jaguars (-9.5) The Colts are a mess; they are playing consecutive road games, and they haven't won at Jacksonville since 2014, when Andrew Luck was the quarterback. Oh, and they traded their best offensive lineman, Quentin Nelson. The Jaguars are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. This one will get ugly as the Jaguars bounce back from the loss to the Texans in London. Pick: Jaguars 30, Colts 16 Los Angeles Chargers (+6.5) at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The battle of Los Angeles isn't quite the game many expected before the season. The Chargers, coming off a bye, haven't won yet and the Rams have been a disappointment. But the Rams won last week at Las Vegas to seemingly right things. They will win here, but the rested Chargers will keep it close. Pick: Rams 23, Chargers 20 Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5) at Denver Broncos Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Chiefs' offense was lifeless in Seattle on Sunday night and now faces a tough Denver defense. They have to find ways to get the running game going again with Kenneth Walker. Bo Nix showed some life last week in the victory over Arizona, but this Chiefs defense will be a challenge. Look for a low-scoring game won by Kansas City, with Walker getting going against Denver's defense, which gives up 4.6 yards per rush. Pick: Chiefs 19, Broncos 14 New England Patriots (-7) at Miami Dolphins The Dolphins won their first game last week and have been in a lot of their losses. But this New England team will be a challenge, even at home. The Patriots are coming off a bad road loss to the Bears, and they will be rested, having played on Thursday. The defense limits the Dolphins' offense, and Drake Maye will play well. New England wins it. Pick: Pats 28, Dolphins 14 Philadelphia Eagles at Washington Commanders (-5.5) Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This might be an elimination game of sorts for these two. Both need a victory in the worst way — even in their horrible division. The Eagles are crippled by injuries, but Washington has plenty of their own. With the Eagles on a short week off a Monday night game and the Commanders off a bye, Washington will win it. Pick: Commanders 28, Eagles 16 Chicago Bears at Seattle Seahawks (-3) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are riding high behind Caleb Williams and an improved defense. But this is a tough road trip against a Seattle team that showed what it can do on defense by shutting down the Chiefs Sunday night. Seattle also got the running game going. The Seattle defense will slow down the Chicago offense, and the Seahawks will win it. Green Bay fell to 4-3 with a loss to Detroit in Week 7, and it's in last place in a loaded NFC North through seven weeks. Meanwhile, the Panthers (3-3) are in first place in the NFC South despite a major blowout loss at home against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday. Carolina made the playoffs in the 2025 season, but it has a ton of injuries on both sides of the ball that make it a tough team to trust against other quality opponents -- like Green Bay. Oddsmakers agree with that sentiment, as they've set the Packers as favorites at home to open this week. Panthers vs. Packers Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Panthers +3.5 (-110) Packers -3.5 (-110) Panthers: +154 Packers: -185 48.5 (Over -105/Under -115) There hasn't been a ton of movement in the odds for this game , as the Packers remain 3.5-point favorites at home. The total has jumped up from 47.5 to 48.5 while the moneyline has actually moved in Carolina's favor. According to DraftKings, just 22 percent of the moneyline bets and 41 percent of the spread bets are on the Panthers after their Week 7 showing against Tampa Bay. Earlier this week, I shared in SI Betting's preview for this game why I believe Green Bay is a worthwhile bet: The Panthers’ run defense was torched in Week 7 by Tampa Bay, and this could be a “get-right” spot for Matt LaFleur’s offense. Love should be able to attack through the air, as the Panthers are a below-average defense overall (20th in EPA/Play), and they entered Week 7 allowing the most yards per carry in the league. Meanwhile, Green Bay’s defense held a vaunted Detroit offense to just 20 points and is now fifth in the league in EPA/Play. If it weren’t for multiple missed field goals, the Pack could be entering this game with a 5-2 record. Carolina beat Detroit this season, but it has some confounding losses against Cleveland and at home against Tampa Bay. I don’t love this team – which is extremely banged up after Taylor Moton went down in Week 7 – on a short week against a Packers squad that has an above-average defense. I’m going to lay the points with a Green Bay team that needs this game a lot more than Carolina does if it’s going to make the playoffs. I'm not the only member of the SI Betting team taking Green Bay, as Iain MacMillan shared in his Road to 272 column -- where he bets on every NFL game, every week -- why he likes the Pack at home as well: I wrote about how I was out on the Panthers last week, and I proved to be right as they ended up on the wrong side of a blowout against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. I'm still out on this Panthers team, as they seem like a significant regression candidate after a strong start to the season. Bryce Young, up until last week, had been playing leaps and bounds better than he had the previous three seasons, and I'm of the belief that it's more of a sign of an abnormally strong start against some bad defenses as opposed to a quarterback who improved by tenfold in a single offseason. The Packers' defense ranks 12th in opponent EPA per play and 10th in opponent EPA per dropback, so with them being on their home field on a short week, I expect them to get to Young in this game. There's always a chance these odds move further as the week goes on, so make sure to hang with the SI Betting team for the latest updates, player prop picks, final game predictions and more for Thursday Night Football in Week 8. The vibes were so high and the Panthers were favored at home before dropping the egg of all eggs against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Now, a loss puts them below .500, souring what had been a really fun start to the season. Will they lose? Here's what the early odds say for this primetime bout. However, drops have kept Matthew Golden from making the most of that involvement, as he's caught just a dozen of those balls. Last week, Golden played through shoulder pain and finished with six catches on 12 targets for just 39 yards receiving in the loss to Detroit. He's listed on the injury report with that same shoulder issue, as well as a foot ailment, ahead of this quick turnaround. On top of those injuries, this matchup with the Carolina Panthers is a tough one. Carolina doesn't allow many explosive plays (the second-fewest pass plays of 20-plus yards) and ranks third-lowest in targets to WR2s, while allowing the fifth-fewest yards to that position. The Panthers also limit air yards to rival receivers. Golden leads Green Bay in air yards per reception, but with the Packers' offensive line missing plenty of pieces, quarterback Jordan Love won't have time in the pocket for deeper routes to develop. Love is already feeling pressure at the ninth-highest rate per dropback and stares down a Carolina pass rush ranked sixth in pressure rate and in blitz percentage. Some of Golden's projections for Thursday night flirt with 70 receiving yards, but most models come in lower, with a low of 48. My number sits at 63 yards for the second-year WR, but I lean toward the Under given the matchup and injury concerns. Prop pick #2: Jalen Coker 5+ receptions Carolina receiver Jalen Coker practiced in full ahead of TNF and draws a favorable matchup against this Packers' pass defense. Coker is the Panthers' WR2 and has had solid success out of the slot, especially against zone coverage. Heading into Week 8, Coker leads Carolina's receiving corps in PFF rating against zone coverage (20th among all WRs). Green Bay runs one of the higher rates of zone defense and has allowed an NFL-high 7.7 average targets to WR2s. Coker is coming off a quiet Week 7 in which he drew only four targets and caught one pass. However, he played fewer snaps in the second half of a blowout loss to Tampa Bay, finishing with only 37. He's played a bigger role in previous games. Coker had at least nine targets in three of his four previous outings, reeling in six, eight, and eight catches, respectively. Projections for Thursday all lean toward five or more receptions, with my number at 5.2. Prop pick #3: Bryce Young 1+ interceptions Bryce Young has been working hard to shed his "bust" label over the past two seasons. Games like Week 7's defeat don't help. Carolina's QB went 14-for-27 for just 163 yards and threw two interceptions vs. Tampa Bay. He has little time to shake off that stink before traveling to Lambeau Field for TNF. That quick turnaround also leaves little time to patch holes in the Panthers' pass protection, with OT Taylor Moton lost for the season this past Sunday and LG Damien Lewis listed as questionable. Young was already facing pressure at the second-highest rate per dropback among all QBs. Those collapsing pockets have translated into hurried throws and accuracy issues. He has the fifth-highest bad-throw rate and the 15th-lowest on-target percentage. The Packers are a top-10 pass defense in advanced metrics like DVOA and EPA allowed per dropback, and they've benefited from a league-best nine interceptions. Several models put Young's interception probability at 70% or higher, and given Carolina's pass-positive game script as a road underdog, I agree with the high side of those projections. Carolina Panthers Add Two Key Players to Injury Report - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Carolina Panthers Add Two Key Players to Injury Report (REUTERS) Zack Pearson Tue, October 27, 2026 at 3:55 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Carolina Panthers saw their two-game win streak snapped at the hands of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday . It was an embarrassing performance for the Panthers at home, allowing Tampa Bay to do whatever they wanted in that game. Carolina left the game 3-3 and having a lot of questions still to be answered. The good news? They have a quick turnaround as they will head to Green Bay to face off against the Packers. The bad news? Green Bay is a good team and the Panthers will enter this game banged up. As the team returned to the practice field for a walk-through on Monday, there were some notable names on the injury report. The most notable additions are on the offensive side of the football with guard Damien Lewis and Jalen Coker. Lewis was added to the injury report with a knee injury. He missed the Detroit game with an elbow injury but returned to play against both Philadelphia and Tampa Bay. Now, a knee injury could limit his ability all week and his chances to play at Green Bay. away.blurb: After missing three games due to a dislocated thumb on his throwing hand, quarterback Baker Mayfield is back in the lineup for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday as they take on the Carolina Panthers in a critical intra-division game. Mayfield carried a questionable designation on the injury report into the weekend but was able to practice without limitations throughout the week. He intends to wear a specialized glove on his right hand that offers added support to the injured joint, preventing the thumb from being bent backward. Mayfield will not have the team's top receiving target at his disposal, however, as wide receiver Emeka Egbuka is out for Week Seven with both a concussion and a foot injury. In addition, starting right tackle Luke Goedeke is out due to a calf ailment and safety Antoine Winfield Jr. will miss his third straight outing thanks to a rib fracture. The Buccaneers and Panthers submitted their list of inactives at 11:32 a.m. ET on Sunday, 90 minutes before the scheduled kickoff of their Week Seven meeting at Bank of America Stadium. After elevating linebacker Caden Fordham from the practice squad, the Buccaneers had 54 available players and thus had to name six inactives to get down to the game-day limit of 48. The Panthers also elevated outside linebacker Nick Hampton and cornerback Robert Rochell from the practice squad and had to name seven inactive players. Carolina will be without one of its top pass-rushers as Jaelan Phillips is out due to a hamstring strain. Fellow outside linebacker Thomas Incoom is also unavailable due to a calf issue, and he was placed on injured reserve on Saturday. away.blurb: So can the Panthers sustain their recent success? Will Mayfield’s return yield a new hope? Will the NFC South standings be shaken up? Fans can also check the game out on radio: WRFX The Fox, 99.7 FM. Anish Shroff (play-by-play), Luke Kuechly (analyst), Jake Delhomme (analyst), Jim Szoke (host), Kristen Balboni (sideline). For full local listings, check out the Carolina Panthers Radio Network . Special note: Kuechly will receive his Pro Football Hall of Fame ring at halftime of the game in Bank of America Stadium. Out: OLB Thomas Incoom (calf), OLB Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) Questionable: OT Monroe Freeling (knee), LB Bam Martin-Scott (hamstring) Out: WR Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot), OT Luke Goedeke (calf), S Antoine Winfield (rib) Questionable: QB Baker Mayfield (right thumb) Alex Zietlow: Panthers 35, Bucs 31. I know that Baker Mayfield’s almost-certain return will make this Bucs offense more dynamic. And I know that scoring 35 on this Bucs team will be difficult, considering their opportunistic defensive backfield and their Top 5 rush defense. Still, barring an implosion of turnovers, I think the Panthers outscore and outlast a Bucs team trying to get back on track. Can the Carolina Panthers make it three wins in a row? And can the Tampa Bay Buccaneers get back on track? The Panthers (3-2) are returning to Bank of America Stadium for their Week 7 contest (1 p.m., FOX) fresh off two statement victories against the Detroit Lions and the Philadelphia Eagles . They’re looking to go 4-2 for the first time as a franchise since 2019 and start 2-0 in the NFC South for the first time since 2022. Carolina ranks first in the NFL in passing yards per game (295.6), second in total yards per game (404.4) and fourth in points per game (29.2). And its defense — minus the Week 1 fiasco against the Bears that’s looking more and more like an aberration — is Top 10 in several statistics, including rushing yards allowed. The Panthers have allowed fewer than 50 yards in each of the last two weeks: 46 against the Lions, 35 against the Eagles. It’s true that the defense is a bit affected by injury, specifically at the outside linebacker spot with no Jaelan Phillips or Thomas Incoom this week . It’s also true that the defense has only had to play against starting quarterbacks three times so far this season, and two of those three — against Caleb Williams of the Bears and Deshaun Watson of the Browns — have yielded losses. That won’t happen this week; it looks like the Bucs will be led by Baker Mayfield, who’s missed the last few weeks with a dislocated thumb on his throwing hand. Speaking of the Bucs (1-5): While many of their offensive stats might be skewed by Mayfield’s absence, many of their strengths will remain. Namely? Their rush defense. Tampa Bay ranks second in the NFL in rush yards allowed per game at 75.5, thanks to a defensive line anchored by nose tackle Vita Vea and an entire unit led by rookie linebacker Josiah Trotter. The Bears' defense will keep them in it with some sacks and takeaways vs. Sam Darnold. In a lower-scoring affair in prime time, go with the team backed by a loud home crowd. Pick: Seahawks win 23-20 but fail to cover the spread. Bo Nix has been a great home QB but Patrick Mahomes also has a history of owning the Broncos . This should be a hard-fought physical game but Kansas City's running game will provide the winning edge. Pick: Chiefs win 23-20 and cover the spread. Lock of the Week: Colts at Jaguars (-7.5, 46.5 o/u) Odds: -111 on bet365 Probability: 52.15% on ProphetX Sunday 1 p.m. ET, CBS The Jaguars are an interception-hungry defense under Anthony Campanile. Daniel Jones is struggling with ball protection and making bad decisions like he did in his Giants ' days. Jacksonville will be ready to fly out of the gate after a Week 7 bye, while Indianapolis is reeling and almost going through the motions with lame-duck coach Shane Steichen. The Jaguars also are No. 1 against the run, making it tougher sledding for Jonathan Taylor. Pick: Jaguars win 31-14 and cover the spread. You never know what you'll get, especially when division rivals play each other, regardless of who's home and who's away. We think the Buccaneers (routing the Panthers on the road) were impressive in Week 7, but the Falcons made the bigger statement (beating the 49ers at home). That's all we've got and we're going with it. Pick: Falcons win 27-24. Ravens at Bills (-3.5, 53.5 o/u) Odds: -104 on bet365 Probability: 48.08% on ProphetX The Bills have more issues with pass defense, but whether it's Tyler Huntley or Lamar Jackson, the Ravens give them a break with their inconsistency. Derrick Henry has been a Bills killer in the past, but Baltimore's rushing attack is slumping. Arizona, on the flipside, cannot cover or contain Dak Prescott's weapons downfield. Pick: Cowboys win 30-20 and cover the spread. away.headline: Ravens QB Lamar Jackson expected to play in Week 8: report
away.blurb: Jackson was able to notch limited practice participation leading up to this past Sunday’s Week 7 loss to the Bengals, but he was ultimately ruled out. Now, the Ravens are gearing up for a highly-anticipated Week 8 matchup against the Buffalo Bills. Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson has missed each of the last three games after suffering an ankle injury in Week 4. The Ravens are 1-2 over that span with Tyler Huntley at the helm, dropping each of their last two games against the division-rival Cleveland Browns and Cincinnati Bengals. On Tuesday, NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport confidently reported that Jackson will be on the field for this Week 8 clash. “I expect, based on the people that I’ve spoken with, that Lamar Jackson will play this week. He will be on the field this week against the Buffalo Bills,” Rapoport said. “I know we’ve been here before. This was a 2-3 week injury — he’s through the third week. He is believed to be as close to 100% as he has been and the Ravens do expect him to play.” With Jackson off the field, the Ravens have dropped to last place in the AFC North standings with a 4-3 record. They’ll look to get back in the win column in a difficult road matchup against the Bills this coming Sunday. Sunday’s game will kick off at 1 p.m. ET. The Ravens then have a short week to prepare for a “Thursday Night Football” matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 9. away.blurb: Ravens Week 7 Injury Report: Lamar Jackson Officially Limited - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Ravens Week 7 Injury Report: Lamar Jackson Officially Limited Despite quarterback Lamar Jackson not practicing during the media portion of practice, he apparently did some limited work. As stated above, Jackson practiced in a limited fashion . Head coach Jesse Minter also said the quarterback did some work with the team as well. Jackson was officially limited with his ankle. Whether or not that means he can play on Sunday remains to be seen. The good news for the Ravens is that the passer was limited, as opposed to not practicing. Wide receiver Rashod Bateman (shoulder), safety Jaylinn Hawkins (knee), tight end Matthew Hibner (hand), guard Vega Ioane (ankle), guard John Simpson (groin), tackle Ronnie Stanley (rest, toe, ankle), cornerback T.J. Tampa (knee), guard Andrew Vorhees (foot), and defensive lineman Broderick Washington (ankle) were all limited. If Ioane's ankle leads to him being ruled out, it would lead to Vorhees potentially taking over. However, Vorhees is also dealing with a foot injury that has led to him missing the last two games. If the worst-case scenario happens for the Ravens' line, it would be Emery Jones Jr. stepping in yet again as the team's right guard. Jones has filled in with Ioane stepping in at center and Vorhees being out due to injury. (Tommy Gilligan-Imagn Images) James Brizuela Thu, October 22, 2026 at 3:37 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Baltimore Ravens are gearing up to face the Cincinnati Bengals, and the team has released its initial injury report. The full injury report is as follows: The only two players who did not participate on Wednesday is veteran defensive lineman Calais Campbell, who had veteran rest, and linebacker Tavius Robinson, who is dealing with a pectoral injury. Hibner has returned to practice after missing Week 6 due to a hand injury. A bigger issue is Ioane appearing on the injury report with an ankle ailment. He has served as the team's emergency center, but it does appear that Cam Jurgens is returning. Jurgens did not have a red no-contact jersey on at practice, and Minter stated the team is "excited" to get him on the field as the team's center. If Jurgens can line up as the team's center, that would lead to Ioane returning to the right guard position. This is assuming that Ioane can also suit up. Some better news is that Tampa is also working his way back from injury. The cornerback suffered a knee injury in Week 1 that has sidelined him since then. Baltimore has an important matchup with the Cincinnati Bengals. Losing two divisional matchups might come back to haunt the Ravens at the end of the season.

home.blurb: Brown getting the benefit of a bye week to rest the back injury he assured us was just some soreness and something he tweaked after a long plane ride out west, may not have been enough. Now he is saying he rested through practice in Week 6 so he would be available when the Bills faced the Las Vegas Raiders. He is still sore, still resting – three weeks later. Sure, it would have been nice to think a week of no football would heal them, but realistically, we may see them on this list all year. So, limited to start the week is a positive. The Buffalo Bills got back to work on Wednesday. The hope has widely been that the bye week would give some added rest to players who had been nursing bumps, bruises, and those injuries that were keeping them from going full speed. home.headline: NFL rescinds Buffalo Bills defender's one-game spitting suspension
home.blurb: The Buffalo Bills ' secondary won't be as depleted in Week 8 as they might have expected. Sam Franklin Jr.'s suspension for allegedly spitting at an opponent during the Bills ' Week 6 win over the Las Vegas Raiders has been overturned following his appeal. Matt Signora, the NFL's senior vice president of football and international communications, announced on Friday, Oct. 23 that a hearing officer had reduced Franklin's punishment from a suspension to a fine. "Hearing officer James Thrash, jointly appointed by the NFL and the NFLPA, has reduced the discipline of Sam Franklin from a one-game suspension to a fine of $14,926 for unsportsmanlike conduct," Signora wrote on social media site X. GARDNER-JOHNSON: Suspended Bills player apologizes after ejection for spitting on Raiders star Prior to his overturned suspension, Franklin was set to be the second Bills player suspended for spitting at an opponent during Buffalo's Week 6 game. Teammate and fellow defensive back C.J. Gardner-Johnson was ejected from the matchup and suspended for the Bills' next game in Week 8 after spitting at Raiders tight end Brock Bowers . Gardner-Johnson has since apologized . According to the NFL's initial version of events, Franklin spit at an opponent after Las Vegas kicked an extra point with 1 minute and 32 seconds left in the fourth quarter. As a violation of the NFL's official rules, the defensive back was set to be suspended from Monday, Oct. 26 to Monday, Nov. 2 – the week leading up to and including the Bills' next game after their Week 7 bye. After his appeal and a further review of the incident, Franklin will pay a fine for unsportsmanlike conduct instead of serving his suspension. Conversely, Gardner-Johnson remains suspended for Week 8. Franklin, who signed a three-year, $7.5 million extension in February, is a special teams captain for Buffalo. He has appeared in all six games this season, exclusively on special teams. Prior to joining the Bills last year, he spent the first five years of his career with the Carolina Panthers. home.headline: Buffalo Bills: Four roster moves, one bigger question before Baltimore
home.blurb: The timing matters because Lamar Jackson is expected to return for the Ravens after missing time with an ankle injury. If he plays, Buffalo could face a very different challenge than it would against a Baltimore team without its starting quarterback. The Buffalo Bills have made four roster moves ahead of their Week 8 matchup with the Baltimore Ravens. Two players are back on the practice squad, and two others are looking for work. On the surface, it’s routine NFL business. But with the trade deadline approaching, a bigger question remains: Are the Bills comfortable with the roster they have, or are they still searching for answers? Buffalo released defensive tackle Austin Johnson and cornerback Anthony Kendall while re-signing defensive end Andre Jones Jr. and cornerback A.J. Woods to the practice squad. Johnson has played 145 NFL games over 11 seasons. Kendall had just played 31 snaps against the Los Angeles Rams as a practice squad elevation. That’s a reminder of how quickly things can change in professional football. Experience and opportunity matter, but neither guarantees a roster spot next week. The Bills Have Some Decisions to Make The more interesting part is what comes next. Buffalo has until November 10 to make a deal before the trade deadline, and the team’s needs are becoming harder to ignore. Cornerback, safety and inside linebacker have been identified as possible areas for improvement. There’s also the question of whether the Bills need another receiver, particularly with DJ Moore dealing with a shoulder injury and questions surrounding Joshua Palmer’s production. None of that guarantees a trade. Teams have to weigh the cost of acquiring a player against the money, draft capital and opportunities they’re giving up. Sometimes the best move is to bring in outside help. Sometimes it’s giving a young player another chance to develop. Still, the Bills can’t afford to treat every roster decision as an isolated event. If they believe they can contend, the deadline offers an opportunity to address weaknesses before they become bigger problems. Baltimore Changes the Conversation That puts extra importance on the Bills’ defensive depth. A healthy Jackson can stress a defence in ways that go beyond the passing game, and small weaknesses can become much more noticeable against an opponent who can exploit them. The four roster moves don’t tell us whether Buffalo will make a trade, and they shouldn’t be treated as evidence of panic. But they do arrive at an important point in the season. The Bills have a major test ahead and a deadline approaching. The question isn’t simply who made the roster today. It’s whether Buffalo has enough answers to get where it wants to go — or whether it needs another move before the opportunity passes. Especially after last week’s blown two-score lead to the Cleveland Browns, nobody is expecting Robert Saleh’s first team in Nashville to execute a miraculous turnaround. Draft discussions are already becoming relevant, if that tells you anything. Still, the Titans hit the road to face the Cincinnati Bengals this coming Sunday, and it’s a chance for Tennessee to win their second game in three weeks. That’s somehow still an exciting prospect. To preview the matchup, I’ve got one reason the Titans will beat the Bengals, one reason they won’t, and my own prediction for what will actually happen. Let’s start with the former. Will: Titans’ secondary sees massive uptick Two weeks in a row now, Tennessee has forced at least one interception. The Titans have come down with three picks over the last two games, two of which belong to rising offseason pickup Cor’Dale Flott. Tennessee Titans cornerback Cor'dale Flott (18) intercepts Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones (17) on Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026, at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Bengals score a lot - a lot - of points. TeamRankings has Cincinnati fourth in the NFL in points per game (27.2) and touchdowns per game (3.2). Their passing statistics specifically are top 10 across the board regarding pass play percentage, completion percentage, and pass yards per game. The Bengals score a lot - a lot - of points. TeamRankings has Cincinnati fourth in the NFL in points per game (27.2) and touchdowns per game (3.2). Their passing statistics specifically are top 10 across the board regarding pass play percentage, completion percentage, and pass yards per game. Tennessee is facing one of the best pass-first teams in the NFL. If Saleh's secondary can find consistency beyond the occasional turnover, the Titans would have more than a fair chance to shut down RB Chase Brown on the ground, too. It's much easier to stop Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins in concept than it is on the field, but doing so is the Titans' key to winning this one. Won’t: Titans can't overcome inconsistent Bengals defense The inverse, of course, is if the Titans' offense continues to suffer. The Bengals have proved themselves beatable against "bad" teams - just see their narrow, one-score win over the 1-6 Miami Dolphins two weeks ago. But Cincinnati also just dismantled the Baltimore Ravens last week, 35-13. The through line is that Cincy scored 30+ points in both of those contests; it comes down to the opposing offense's ability to hang in there when Burrow and his crew get hot. Tennessee ranks 31st in both touchdowns and points per game. Almost everywhere the Bengals are in the top 10 through the air, the Titans are in the bottom 10. Cincy has allowed 20+ points in four of their six games this season. If Cam Ward can get back on his feet in any sense of the saying, another 24-point performance like Tennessee had last week could be enough to at least make this one interesting. However, the Titans may need a little more juice than they've seen yet this season from their QB to stay in it. Prediction: Titans lose, 31-20 Ultimately, I have the Titans falling to 1-7 in this one. We've seen a number of trends solidify that this roster has failed to prove their ability to rise beyond. Carnell Tate is the primary receiver in an otherwise underwhelming offense. The defense can force early turnovers, but can't get late stops when it matters - especially when it comes to tackling. Ward has a better second half than his typically abysmal first, but by the time Tennessee tries to get aggressive, it's too late to make a difference. I expect most of, if not all of these notes to be hit in Week 8. I don't think the Titans will lose in a blowout, but on the road against one of the best offenses in the league, this one already looks like too much for Saleh's team. picks.blurb: Titans scouting report vs Cincinnati Bengals, matchups, prediction NFL Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Drew Rasmussen starting Game 5 NFL trade deadline proposals WNBA Finals schedule fiasco Anthony Edwards injury impact Week 8 fantasy trade tips Titans scouting report vs Cincinnati Bengals, matchups, prediction NFL Week 8 Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Positives are hard to find amid the Tennessee Titans' struggles, but running back Tony Pollard was one last week. The Memphis native had his second-best game as a Titans player, with 129 yards rushing and three touchdowns on 25 carries in a gutting 27-24 home loss to the Cleveland Browns on Oct. 25. Maybe Pollard can do it again when the Titans (1-6) face the Cincinnati Bengals (4-2) at Paycor Stadium on Nov. 1 (noon CT, CBS) in NFL Week 8. The Bengals' and Browns ' run defenses are about the same statistically. Cincinnati allows 116.3 rushing yards per game, which ranks 19th in the league. The Titans gained a season-high 322 yards of offense with Pollard's contributions, taking pressure off developing second-year quarterback Cam Ward . Now that unit will face Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow, who's 11th in the league with 1,653 yards passing, and second with 15 passing touchdowns, to go with three interceptions. Here's our scouting report for the Titans' game against the Browns. One Cincinnati Bengals stat to know Cincinnati has 13 pass plays of 25 yards or more this season. Tennessee has seven. Where Tennessee Titans have edge vs. Bengals The good news: Cincinnati's offense ranks 29th in rushing yards per game (81.2), so there's an opportunity for the Titans to make the Bengals one-dimensional. The bad news: Cincinnati's offense is doing fine without a rushing threat, averaging 345.2 yards. It isn't a big Titans advantage, but they must capitalize on it and see if stopping the run allows their pass rush to play like it did against the Colts (six sacks). It will take a stark turnaround after Tennessee allowed a season-high 183 yards rushing against the Browns. That marked the franchise's worst single-game Pro Football Focus run defense grade (36.3) since 2023. Personnel changes up front have not helped. Run-stopping defensive tackle Jordan Elliott was released on Oct. 20 after breaking the NFL's gun policy . Third-year defender Timmy Horne was signed from the practice squad to replace him. Where Cincinnati Bengals have edge vs. Titans Tennessee's secondary tackled poorly and took bad angles against the Browns, making rookie receiver KC Concepcion look like a Pro Bowler (eight catches, 129 yards). Imagine what Burrow and receivers Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase might do. The Titans haven't seen an offense like this in 2026. The Bengals are seventh in the league in passing yards per game (264) and get 76% of their total yards through the air. Higgins and Chase have accounted for nine of the Bengals' 13 explosive pass plays. Saleh's also soul-searching in his secondary. Alontae Taylor was signed in the offseason to fortify one of Tennessee's outside corner spots, but he was made inactive in Week 6 by coach's decision and didn't see the field in Week 7. Now it looks like Taylor will likely move to nickel . This would be a good week for Taylor to make a contribution, assuming Saleh plays him. Score prediction: Bengals 35, Titans 21 The Titans' scarred defense won't be able to slow Burrow, and they can't depend on Ward to keep pace in a shootout. It looks like their worst-case scenario matchup. Winning the turnover battle and making a few plays on special teams would help, but the Titans will be fortunate to keep it within 14 points. The Cincinnati Bengals are coming off a monster win over the Baltimore Ravens , but they cannot afford to let that lead to them overlooking their next opponent, the Tennessee Titans. I know the Titans are 1-6 and are not a good football team. But this is the NFL, where the margin for error is razor-thin, if that. For the Bengals, this is a prime opportunity to squash any sense of this game being a trap game— coming off a dominant road win at Baltimore and going to Madrid in two weeks— and putting their first complete game together this season. Right now, on FanDuel , the Bengals are a 10.5-point favorite against the Titans. Their moneyline is -650, and the over/under is 46.5 points. This will be Tennessee’s first time playing in Cincinnati since 2020. Ironically, that was Week 8 in 2020 and on November 1st. The Bengals won that game 31-20, which was a coming-out party for Joe Burrow in his rookie season. Burrow was 26/37 for 249 yards and two touchdowns in that game, making a featured appearance on the highlights during NBC’s Sunday Night Football game coverage that night. Since that game, the Bengals and Titans have played four times in Nashville, including in the Divisional round of the 2021 NFL Playoffs. That was the game where Joe Burrow overcame nine sacks and willed the Bengals to a 19-16 win that was the first road playoff win in Bengals history. Cincinnati beat Tennessee 37-27 in Week 15 of the 2024 Season, which was the most recent matchup between the two teams. Tennessee’s head coach is Robert Saleh, in his first season with the Titans. He previously coached the New York Jets and served two stints as the San Francisco 49ers’ defensive coordinator. The Titans are 1-6 and coming off a last-second 27-24 loss to the Cleveland Browns in Week 7. Quarterback Cam Ward is in his second season and has thrown for just 1,179 yards and just four touchdowns this season. Ward also has just one game with over 200 passing yards. Entering Sunday, the Titans were in the bottom two in the NFL in both scoring and total offense, while ranking in the middle of the pack in both scoring and total defense. However, the Titans have been competitive most of the season, as four of their six losses came by one score. Two of them were to the division-leading Giants (12-7) and the aforementioned loss to Cleveland. away.headline: Zac Taylor Drops Positive Injury Update to Open Titans Practices
away.blurb: Other than that, Cincinnati doesn't have many injury issues to worry about. Names like WR Andrei Iosivas (finger) and CB Jalen Davis (hamstring) have both been out the minimum four weeks on short-term IR. "I just am really proud of our guys, to be flat out honest with you," Taylor said about beating Baltimore. "I am just proud of the way they responded. When you coach, and you're in that position, and you think you know how they're going to respond, but to just see everybody step up at every position, every coach, and respond that way on the road in the second half – it just makes you really proud, and that's what makes you fired up. It's nothing more than that. It's your team responding the right way and putting together a significant win, and it fires you up." Zac Taylor and his team are running back onto the practice field this afternoon after the Week 7 win over the Baltimore Ravens. Cincinnati unfortunately had to put Erick All (knee) on season-ending injured reserve with his third career torn right ACL, and Kyle Dugger (quad) isn't playing this week against Tennessee. They should be back to normal practices soon. It's just been a horrible few days for All, while Dugger is "week to week" with his injury. "It's awful for him," Taylor said about All. "He's been through this a couple of times before. We'll be there to support him in his recovery and rehab. But it just sucks for him. This means so much to him. He's worked so hard to get himself back." The Bengals are currently the seventh seed in the AFC as they keep trying to push for an AFC North title. They are 3-2 in the AFC and cannot afford a loss to the one-win Titans. Bottling the second-half output from Sunday and sprinkling it into every game moving forward won't hurt the Bengals' chances of contending this season. Cincinnati's defense has been so much better in 2026 compared to last season. The Bengals rank 11th in the NFL in EPA/play allowed (26th last season). "If we're going to continue to be great in the red zone and really good at short yardage, it's going to be really difficult for people to put points up on the board, and we got to take a lot of pride in that," Taylor said. "And sometimes it's after long drives where you've been on the field for eight minutes, and it's defeating because they've converted third downs and gotten big plays, and you got to overcome adversity, and then you got to just buckle up and hold them to a field goal." Cincinnati takes on the Titans at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday. So, it sounds as though the ankle is a bit sore, but enough to be deemed a legitimate injury. We will see if Chase misses any more time. At that point, it would be a legitimate injury to be concerned about. For now, it appears as though Chase is going to be ready to play in Week 8 against the Tennessee Titans . Cincinnati Bengals Wide Receiver Ja'Marr Chase Appears on Injury Report This early in the week, veteran players can be given time off, and that is no different for Chase. Chase missed five games in 2022 due to a hip injury. Even then, he returned much faster than anticipated. Other than that, he has not missed any time due to an injury. Chase has also gone over 1,000 yards in his first five NFL seasons. Chase produced 1,455 yards as a rookie, making the second-team All-Pro and being named the Offensive Rookie of the Year. In his second season, he played in 12 games and produced 1,046 yards. He bounced back the next year with 1,216 yards on 100 receptions. Then, he had a career year in 2024. Chase put up 127 receptions for 1,708 yards. He was not as good in 2025, but Joe Burrow ended up missing a good chunk of time. Still, he finished with 125 catches for 1,412 yards. So far this season, he has 351 yards. Still, Chase is a bit less productive than in most seasons. He is averaging 1.9 yards per route run. That is strong for most receivers, but not up to the standard of the All-Pro. Chase averaged 2.21 yards per route run for his career, and his career low before this season was 1.97. So, there could be an argument that Chase just needs a day to rest and get back to his old ways. He is not injured, but not quite up to full speed, either. Bengals Enter Week 8 Matchup With Titans Cincinnati is coming into the game with a 4-2 record. They started hot with wins against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Houston Texans . However, they stumbled against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 3. They lost to the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 4, but have now won two straight. However, they beat the 1-5 Miami Dolphins , and Tyler Huntley led the Baltimore Ravens . Now, they get the 1-6 Tennessee Titans. They need to rack up the wins because the Atlanta Falcons and Pittsburgh Steelers present bigger tests in Weeks 9 and 10. home.headline: Ja’Marr Chase injury update is concerning start to week for Bengals WR
home.blurb: It appears Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja’Marr Chase is on injury watch at the outset of Week 8. According to The Athletic’s Mike Petraglia , Chase was not spotted at practice during the portion open to the media on Wednesday. “Bengals stretch on a perfect Wednesday outside Paycor. No Ja’Marr Chase spotted at stretch,” Petraglia wrote. This means that Chase is on track to be a non-participant in practice to begin the week, which puts his status in question. MORE: NFL MVP odds entering Week 8 As of this writing, it isn’t clear what Chase is dealing with that has him sidelined. The superstar wide receiver was not listed on Cincinnati’s injury report last week. We’ll have our answer later in the day, when the Bengals release their first injury report. The good news is, Chase will have two more days to get back on the practice field and avoid a designation before the Bengals take on the Tennessee Titans on Sunday. Bengals’ shaky wide receiver depth If Chase keeps trending in the wrong direction, it’s going to take a village to replace one of the league’s very best wideouts. The problem, however, is that the Bengals don’t have many reliable villagers. Tee Higgins is rock-solid and would step into the role as the Bengals’ No. 1 wide receiver if Chase is forced to sit. Higgins is having a phenomenal season with 571 receiving yards and two scores in six games. He has been especially hot of late after tallying 11 catches for 157 yards in Week 4 and six catches for 148 yards and a touchdown in Week 7 MORE: NFL could learn something from MLB’s success with ABS In all, Higgins ranks eighth in the NFL in receiving yards and actually has more than Chase, who has tallied 351. The problem is: who steps up behind him? Andrei Iosivas is on injured reserve and the Bengals have a slew of wild cards in their receivers room with guys like Dohnte Meyers, Colbie Young and Mitch Tinsley. With that group, Mike Gesicki’s contribution will be crucial.

home.blurb: Chase (ankle) officially had a rest day, but is also listed with an ankle injury. He was seen in the locker room after practice. The “rest” being listed as the primary reason for his DNP insinuates it is not a serious injury, but seeing what the rest of his week looks like will be key before Sunday's game. Safety Kyle Dugger (quad) aggravated his quad injury during last Sunday's win over the Baltimore Ravens and is back to being “week-to-week.” Coach Zac Taylor has already declared Dugger out for this week. Defensive tackle Jonathan Allen got his usual rest day. S Jordan Battle was limited with a hamstring injury, which he's been playing through for the last month. Linebacker Joe Giles-Harris (calf) was also limited. Four Titans did not practice due to injuries including their first-round pick, WR Carnell Tate (shoulder). Tate has played in all seven games for Tennessee this season, catching 34 passes for 413 yards and a touchdown. Fellow receiver Calvin Ridley (hip) went limited. He's been dealing with his hip injury for the last week and missed last Sunday's game because of it. DT John Franklin-Myers (groin) was also a DNP. He's been playing next to All-Pro Jeffery Simmons and has produced 13 pressures and 1.5 sacks in seven games. away.headline: Cardinals' Michael Wilson Gets Surprising Week 8 Practice Update
away.blurb: This would be a massive blow for the Cardinals' offense if Wilson isn't available. ARIZONA — There were a handful of notable Arizona Cardinals missing from the team's Wednesday practice , and though Michael Wilson wasn't one, we did get a surprising update during the period open to reporters. Wilson was spotted wearing a yellow non-contact jersey on Wednesday, which signals Wilson is dealing with an injury. In public knowledge he emerged clean from Week 7's loss to the Denver Broncos and didn't appear to be dealing with any injuries, nor did head coach Mike LaFleur mention anything about Wilson in his morning press conference. Players wearing this jersey signals to teammates that he cannot be blocked or hit. While this doesn't automatically mean Wilson is in concussion protocol, players progressing through protocol are typically the ones that don the non-contact jerseys during practice. Reporters are not able to ask LaFleur about his status until Friday when he holds his next press conference. The Cardinals travel to face the Dallas Cowboys in Week 8. Arizona will reveal their first injury report of the week later today, which will provide us clarity on what exactly Wilson is dealing with. Wilson's production has slowed down a bit since Marvin Harrison Jr. was traded, which is something LaFleur was specifically asked about earlier this week: “I think if you take away the stats from it, he’s running good routes and he’s separating. He has drawn quite a few penalties this year as well. I mean that got us going there on that third drive (of the game). With that being said, I know he can still make that play — for himself too, but (it’s) just kind of the momentum of making a play as opposed to a penalty," LaFleur said, reflecting back on his performance against the Broncos. "I mean he (Broncos CB Riley Moss) held him. We told the official it was going to be a double move. He ran the double move. It was a really good route and the guy held him. That was clearly a penalty, but again, I know we can make that play. Then he drew another one a little bit later, but our pocket collapsed right away. To me, when we’re clicking on all cylinders, those are touchdowns. He ran right by the guy off the double move. He’s doing a lot of good things. He obviously hasn’t had the stats and that’s kind of what you’re insinuating right there. "Again, all he can do is control what he can control — win his one-on-one matchups when the ball’s thrown to him, catch it, and then obviously try to stay grounded and make as much ‘YAC’ (yards after the catch) as he can.” Walter Nolen III Gets Injury Update Ahead of Cardinals-Cowboys 7 Alarming Stats the Cardinals Must Fix Immediately Cardinals WR Reveals He's Having Season-Ending Surgery 13 Winners, Losers From Cardinals' Shocking Win vs Rams Cardinals RB Jeremiyah Love Gets Exciting Week 8 Injury Update This article was originally published on www.si.com/nfl/cardinals/onsi as Cardinals' Michael Wilson Gets Surprising Week 8 Pract

away.headline: Jeremiyah Love injury: Arizona Cardinals RB expected to miss Week 7
away.blurb: Love did not practice all last week and did not play against the Los Angeles Rams . He was a non-participant in practice on Wednesday. It sounds like he will sit the rest of this week as well. On Wednesday, coach Mike LaFleur indicated the Cardinals are focused on getting him right. "He's feeling better, but it kind of goes without saying — (We're) not going to put him out there until he feels 100%." Jeremiyah Love injury: Arizona Cardinals RB expected to miss Week 7 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Jeremiyah Love injury: Arizona Cardinals RB expected to miss Week 7 Jess Root, Cardinals Wire Thu, October 22, 2026 at 6:00 PM UTC · 1 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Arizona Cardinals do not expect to have rookie running back Jeremiyah Love back in Week 7. According to Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports , Love is expected to miss the Cardinals' game against the Denver Broncos on Sunday. Love has been dealing with a lingering ankle injury for weeks. It is not the same ankle he sprained in the preseason. That ankle has healed, and he is not impacted by that. He has played in five games this season. He has rushed for 245 yards and a touchdown, averaging 3.7 yards per attempt. With no Love expected on Sunday, Tyler Allgeier will start and Bam Knight will play in Love's place. Knight rushed for 80 yards against the Rams in Week 6. Evan Hull will likely get elevated from the practice squad. Cardinals' Injury Report is Downright Ugly Skip to main content SI.COM ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals revealed their Thursday injury report for Week 7's clash against the Denver Broncos — and it's not pretty. Darius Robinson and Jon Gaines were added to an already lengthy list of Cardinals that featured Walter Nolen, Budda Baker and Jeremiyah Love among others. Cardinals Thursday Injury Report FULL : Isaac Seumalo (rest), Josh Sweat (rest), Jedrick Wills (illness), The Cardinals, hoping to again play the role of spoiler against Denver, could be massively shorthanded in making that happen as numerous stars are staring down a legitimate possibility of missing time. Baker, Love, Wingard and Nolen have all missed consecutive days of practice now for Arizona. With the Cardinals hoping to take advantage of a disfunctional Broncos offense, Arizona's defense needs all hands on deck. “Last few years. They’re very smart. They’re very well coached," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said of the Broncos' defense. "I have as much respect for ‘VJ’ (Broncos Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph) as anyone in this league. They do it their own way. I don’t want to say they’re not with the times — whatever that means but it’s got an old-school approach to it in terms of some of their coverage and that’s a credit to them. You can tell ‘VJ’ and those guys believe in what they believe in and they’re unapologetic with it. "They play really hard. I see 11 guys working in unison. It’s a challenge. home.blurb: Dallas Goedert is good to go for Monday, while Saquon Barkley and Jalyx Hunt inch closer to a potential return. "It's just kind of the same injury that I sustained earlier. "I want to be out there anytime I can. We only get 17 games. To miss a game, to miss two games, it always stinks. So if I can be available, I'm going to do everything I can to play. "I'm going to go out there and do whatever I can to help the team win, whether it's run blocking, pass blocking, or hopefully get a couple catches. Two of the Eagles' top receivers, DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), have been ruled out, leaving rookie first-round pick Makai Lemon as the primary wide receiver option. "It's definitely a big opportunity with the team," Lemon said. "I'm just super excited to go out there with the guys, put on a good performance. Had a great week of practice with all the guys. So, just trying to go out there and execute. A couple guys are out. So really just, next man up. I got a bunch of trust in the guys next to me, trust in the coaches and the game plan." Running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) took a step forward and was a full participant at practice on Saturday after being limited previously in the week. The running back is listed as questionable for Monday night. Meanwhile, Jonathan Greenard (ankle), who did not practice again on Saturday, is listed as questionable. The edge rusher said it will be a game-time decision as he will need to see how his ankle feels. Alongside Greenard, the outside linebacker room is banged up. Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) could return on Monday as he is listed as questionable after practicing in a limited capacity all week. Nolan Smith (concussion) has been officially ruled out. Smith is joined by defensive back Michael Carter II (abdomen). Cornerback Jakorian Bennett, tight end Grant Calcaterra, guard Landon Dickerson, and tight end Eli Stowers all participated fully in practice on Saturday. They are all listed as questionable since they are on Injured Reserve and would need to be activated by Monday afternoon in order to play against the Cowboys. Pickens headlines the group of limited participants in practices, along with the likes of starting cornerback Cobie Durant (hamstring), starting left tackle Tyler Guyton (calf), and outside linebacker Marist Liufau, who was designated to return from injured reserve and is currently in his 21-day window. home.headline: Cowboys-Eagles final injury update has 7 ruled out including Smith
home.blurb: Running back Saquon Barkley is on track to appear for the first time since leaving the Week 4 game early, and should bring a huge boost to a running game that has floundered the last three weeks. Hopefully ready to meet him in the hole is linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, who hasn't seen action since Week 1 for the Cowboys. The Cowboys also expect CB Cobie Durant to return to action, and he hasn't played since Week 2. Those are two big additions for Dallas. Things are trending right for several other Cowboys, though they aren't quite ready to return to action. The Cowboys opened the 21-day practice window for LB Marist Liufau and safety PJ Locke. Both were expected to be key reserves this year and still could be activated before Monday's game, with corresponding roster moves. Starting safety Jalen Thompson can have his window opened next week. Meanwhile, Dallas did rule out WR/KR Kavontae Turpin (ribs) and LB Dee Winters (calf), along with OT Drew Shelton. McKee won't have his top two receivers as both DeVonta Smith and Dontarin Wycks have been ruled out. Barkley is one of seven listed as questionable, along with OF Landon Dickerson and edge rusher Jonathan Greenard, who is expected to be a game-time decision . Entering their Week 7 Monday Night Football matchup, the teams sport identical 2-4 records after six games , with injuries the underlying factor of both club's malaise. Dallas, implementing a new defense under first-year coordinator Christian Parker, has seen their back-seven progressively decimated week by week, undermining his attempt to get his footing as a scheme designer and playcaller. The Eagles have just lost body after body throughout their roster, losing key contributors to the offense. Are the clubs trending in opposite directions despite losing streaks for both ? Injury wise, Dallas is starting to get some contributors back, with the question being about whether they can actually make a difference or is Parker's scheme a bad one. The Eagles are trending down, still, though they will get a big boost from one returning member. For Philly, the injury discussion has centered around QB Jalen Hurts and the controversy over his blood clot diagnosis . Regardless of the inner workings there, he's been moved to IR and is done for the year, opening the door for Tanner McKee to get the start and raising the possibility if he flounders, the Eagles could turn to Joe Milton III at QB. Philly snatched him off of Dallas' practice squad last week . Here's a look at the complete injury report from Saturday.

I picked every dog against the spread last week and it looked good early, but then it collapsed late with five straight losses, including both prime-time games Sunday and Monday night. I was 8-6 straight up last week and 6-7-1 against the spread. Hey, the spread record was an improvement, which tells you how bad I've been this season. My ATS record this year is 43-61-3, which is a long way from .500. My straight-up record is 62-44-1. So this week, it's back to just picking the games. Forget all dogs. Trying to get to .500 makes me borrow a coaching cliché they all use. One game at a time. One week at a time. Turnaround time. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime These two are both coming off losses. The Carolina loss featured the Bucs running over them for 258 rushing yards. It's been a problem all year. But the Packers don't run it very well, so something has to give. Carolina gave Jordan Love fits last year, but that will change here. Carolina gives up 27.7 points per game. Love lights them up and Josh Jacobs gets the run game going. Pick: Packers 31, Panthers 24 Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Lamar Jackson could be back for the Ravens, but how much will his injured ankle impact his ability to move? The Bills are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. Baltimore's defense was bad in the loss to the Bengals last week, but Buffalo's defense has been awful. Look for a shootout here with Josh Allen getting the best of it. Pick: Bills 35, Ravens 30 Tennessee Titans at Cincinnati Bengals (-10.5) The Titans are having major problems on offense, while the Bengals lit up the Ravens last week. Joe Burrow was special in the second half of that game and I think that will carry over here. Look for an offensive explosion from the Bengals as Burrow starts to get into the MVP talk. Pick: Bengals 36, Titans 10 Arizona Cardinals at Dallas Cowboys (-6.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys' offense came alive against the Eagles Monday night, especially on the ground, which isn't a good thing for an Arizona defense that is last in the league in scoring. The Dallas offense should roll and the Arizona offense won't be able to keep up. Dallas big — even on a short week. Pick: Cowboys 37, Cardinals 21 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) The undefeated Vikings face a tough road game here against Detroit. The Lions offense against the Minnesota defense will be a treat to watch. Jared Goff is playing at a high level right now, but Minnesota's defense is the best in the league in terms of scoring. The Vikings offense is limited, but the Detroit defense has had major problems. But they were better last week, which I think carries over. Lions take it. Pick: Lions 23, Vikings 13 Las Vegas Raiders at New York Jets (-1.5) Kirk Cousins stays in as the starter for the Raiders, but teams have blitzed him the past two weeks. That could be a problem here since the Jets are a top-10 team in blitz percentage. The Raiders have struggled to stop opposing offenses, giving up 28.1 points per game, so look for Geno Smith to have success. Jets win it. Pick: Jets 27, Raiders 16 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) This is a big game for the division lead in the AFC North. The Browns beat the Steelers earlier this year, but this will be a bigger challenge on the road. They are also playing consecutive road games, which will be a challenge. Look for Aaron Rodgers to play well as the Steelers take it. Pick: Steelers 24, Browns 20 Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-2.5) This is suddenly a big game in the NFC South with the Bucs upsetting Carolina last week and the Falcons upsetting the 49ers. The Tampa Bay running game has come alive, but Atlanta is stingy on the ground, giving up 3.8 per rush. That will mean this is a Baker Mayfield game. Tampa Bay gives up 3.5 per rush, which might make for tough going for Bijan Robinson. That's a problem for the Atlanta offense. Tampa Bay wins it. Pick: Bucs 23, Falcons 17 Indianapolis Colts at Jacksonville Jaguars (-9.5) The Colts are a mess; they are playing consecutive road games, and they haven't won at Jacksonville since 2014, when Andrew Luck was the quarterback. Oh, and they traded their best offensive lineman, Quentin Nelson. The Jaguars are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. This one will get ugly as the Jaguars bounce back from the loss to the Texans in London. Pick: Jaguars 30, Colts 16 Los Angeles Chargers (+6.5) at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The battle of Los Angeles isn't quite the game many expected before the season. The Chargers, coming off a bye, haven't won yet and the Rams have been a disappointment. But the Rams won last week at Las Vegas to seemingly right things. They will win here, but the rested Chargers will keep it close. Pick: Rams 23, Chargers 20 Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5) at Denver Broncos Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Chiefs' offense was lifeless in Seattle on Sunday night and now faces a tough Denver defense. They have to find ways to get the running game going again with Kenneth Walker. Bo Nix showed some life last week in the victory over Arizona, but this Chiefs defense will be a challenge. Look for a low-scoring game won by Kansas City, with Walker getting going against Denver's defense, which gives up 4.6 yards per rush. Pick: Chiefs 19, Broncos 14 New England Patriots (-7) at Miami Dolphins The Dolphins won their first game last week and have been in a lot of their losses. But this New England team will be a challenge, even at home. The Patriots are coming off a bad road loss to the Bears, and they will be rested, having played on Thursday. The defense limits the Dolphins' offense, and Drake Maye will play well. New England wins it. Pick: Pats 28, Dolphins 14 Philadelphia Eagles at Washington Commanders (-5.5) Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This might be an elimination game of sorts for these two. Both need a victory in the worst way — even in their horrible division. The Eagles are crippled by injuries, but Washington has plenty of their own. With the Eagles on a short week off a Monday night game and the Commanders off a bye, Washington will win it. Pick: Commanders 28, Eagles 16 Chicago Bears at Seattle Seahawks (-3) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are riding high behind Caleb Williams and an improved defense. But this is a tough road trip against a Seattle team that showed what it can do on defense by shutting down the Chiefs Sunday night. Seattle also got the running game going. The Seattle defense will slow down the Chicago offense, and the Seahawks will win it. picks.blurb: Vikings vs. Lions bold predictions for NFC North clash in Week 8 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Drew Rasmussen starting Game 5 NFL trade deadline proposals WNBA Finals schedule fiasco Anthony Edwards injury impact Week 8 fantasy trade tips Vikings vs. Lions bold predictions for NFC North clash in Week 8 Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints Tue, October 27, 2026 at 2:38 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads As the Minnesota Vikings plan their next massive blitz, the Detroit Lions ride the wave of a big division win. These teams meet in Week 8, and here are bold predictions for the NFC North clash. It's a critical game for the Lions. The NFC North could end up with only two playoff teams. That's because the 49ers, Seahawks, and Rams still seem like firm bets. And that leaves only one other Wild Card spot. The Lions stand at 4-2 while the Vikings are 6-0. A loss would leave the Lions three games back of first place with nearly half the season in the rearview mirror. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs will rush for 100-plus yards It's tough to throw against the Vikings. They rank No. 2 in the NFL against the pass, allowing just 155 yards per game. And while their run defense is good, it's still the better path to consistently moving the football. Gibbs is fourth in the NFL with 620 yards through six games. Look for the Lions to put a saddle on him against the Vikings. Yes, the Lions are clearly overusing Gibbs already. He's almost on a record pace , according to NBC Sports. "If Gibbs keeps to his current pace of 27.7 touches per game for the entire 17-game season, he'll finish this season with a whopping 470 touches," Michael David Smith wrote. "That would be the second-most in a season in NFL history, second only to former James Wilder, who had 492 touches with the 1984 Buccaneers." Gibbs should get close to that number of touches on the ground alone. He had 29 carries against the Saints and Packers this season. Look for the neighborhood of 25 against the Vikings. He's averaging 4.6 per carry, so that easily puts him over 100. And don't worry about the injury scare late against the Packers, according to mlive.com. During his postgame media session, Lions coach Dan Campbell confirmed that Gibbs is OK and avoided serious injury . "Yeah, we got him checked," Lions head coach Dan Campbell said. "He should be good. That's that whole, 'Is it really worth going down and try to finish the game, or you just go score?' Sometimes I question that. I don't know, maybe we shouldn't just, but all good. It's a good win." Lions will double the Vikings' season average in points allowed For the season, the Vikings are allowing just 12.3 points per game. Over the last three games, they are giving up just 33 points. But the Lions will hit them for 24-plus points. Not only will Gibbs cut loose, but his runs will set up play-action daggers for Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams. This is no timid prediction. The Vikings defense is the real deal. The players will even tell you that , according to The Athletic. "It's a generational group," cornerback Isaiah Rodgers said. "We've got guys who go out and trust the scheme. They trust (Flores and his staff). The stats speak for themselves." Defensive tackle Levi Drake Rodriguez said it is togetherness that brings the good outcomes. "Hopefully, that showed the joy we have on the field with each other," Rodriguez said. "We want to work hard for each other. We want to be right." But the Lions are a different beast. They are king of the offensive jungle for a reason. They rank No. 2 in the NFL with 397.3 yards per game. The NFL used to be a league where great defense would pretty much always shut down a great offense. But the rules have changed. And the Lions will cut loose for a point total the Vikings haven't allowed since 22 in the season opener against the Packers. Vikings QB Kyler Murray will have his best game of the season For all the Lions are on offense, they ain't that on defense. They rank dead last in the league with 391 yards allowed per game. Murray hasn't thrown for 250 yards in a game yet this season. In fact, he hasn't done it since 2024. And he only has three touchdown passes in basically four games played. He missed almost all of the season opener after a first-quarter injury. But the Lions are relatively decent against the run. They are an open gate against the pass. And Murray will take advantage with some chunk plays down the field. Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell is standing behind Murray, according to The Athletic. "I think our guys are very confident that we're not far off," O'Connell said. "The far-off changes a little bit as you go, but I'm very, very confident we'll get it going." One reason for optimism is that Murray has gotten better at play action. The Vikings used play action on nearly half of Murray's dropbacks in Week 7. And Murray hit on eight of 11 passes. There's still hope for Murray. Some people have been writing him off and saying the Vikings should move on, but this is a chance for him to silence critics. picks.blurb: Eleventh hour NFL bold predictions for the Vikings, Broncos and Lions in Week 7 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Drew Rasmussen starting Game 5 NFL trade deadline proposals WNBA Finals schedule fiasco Anthony Edwards injury impact Week 8 fantasy trade tips Eleventh hour NFL bold predictions for the Vikings, Broncos and Lions in Week 7 Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Oliver Fox Sun, October 25, 2026 at 3:22 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Everything in life always comes in a six-pack or a four-pack -beers, yogurt, sticks of butter, value packs of Pokemon cards . Why do we allow the numbers six and four to dominate our lives like this? On this NFL Sunday morning, I'm here to resist with a three-pack of bold predictions as we careen violently toward kickoff. The streets are saying I just didn't have time to make a six-pack, to which I will tell the streets to shut up because they're literally just made of concrete while I am a luminous being, not this crude matter. The NFC North will feature heavily, and I have more words for Bo Nix; should be a three-packtacular time! The Vikings will blow it against the Colts to lose undefeated streak Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray and wide receiver Justin Jefferson | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect But hey, this is bold predictions, not "pick a touchdown favorite to win" predictions, and the ultimate zag here would be to say that the Colts, who have launched an exploratory committee on trading their entire team , shock everyone by inverting the vibes completely. There isn't a great argument for this to happen, otherwise it wouldn't be bold, but there is an argument. The Vikings offense really is terrible; they are 27th in EPA per play ahead of absolute titans like the ... Tennessee Titans, the Miami Dolphins and the Los Angeles Chargers. They have had real difficulty moving the ball with Kyler Murray under center, and have gimmicked their way to wins with timely turnovers and crazy performance from an aggressive defense. I'm not saying that doesn't work (it clearly works), but there's no way it can work this consistently. The Colts need to stabilize behind their strengths: running the football and managing an efficient offensive attack. In Week 6 against the Titans, it felt like they held some emergency war council meeting at halftime where they all pitched their best ideas on how to best lose the game. If the team can just play to its own strengths rather than allow their weaknesses to consume them, they should have a chance. Bo Nix will be benched in the third quarter against Arizona Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect This is what we call putting the "bold" and "prediction" in bold prediction, because I could have just said something like "Bo Nix will play garbage football again and we'll all hop on our podcasts and blogs and wonder what he does," but let's get real cynical. What if the Broncos and Sean Payton lose their patience completely? Bo Nix is not a good quarterback. I don't know if he's bad, but by every metric imaginable and by the evidence of my own two eyeballs he's been remarkably ineffective this year. He can't really throw over the middle and he can't really throw deep down the sideline, so he basically just runs a college offense with a ton of handoffs, screen passes and dumpoffs with a hysterically low average depth of target. I don't think Jarrett Stidham is any better, nor am I one of those clowns constantly canvassing for unproven backups to start with no evidence that they'll be good. What I know is that the Broncos coaching staff agrees with my assessment of Bo Nix -they trust him with nothing, refuse to call any downfield shots and just try to protect, protect, protect for as long as they can while they win the game with runs, field goals and defense. If they somehow fall down big to Arizona, though? Maybe we see some emergency quarterback switch, if for no other reason than to save face with the rest of the team. Lions defense shows improvement off the bye, limits Green Bay in a big win at home Detroit Lions safety Brian Branch | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Lions defense, so far this year, has been USDA-certified garbage. They have yet to hold a team under 20 points, get cleaved by every elite pass-catcher they encounter and had one of the most unprofessional performances I ever did see on Thursday Night Football against the Buffalo Bills in Week 2. But I, in my infinite wisdom, have decided (for some reason) that this all will get better, and it will get better right now. This is for three reasons: First, the Lions are getting Brian Branch back for the first time all year, a keystone defensive player and the kind of guy they've been missing all season. Second, they're at home, and home field still really matters in football for defensive performance -the only sport where it still really means anything. Third and finally is simple mathematical regression. No defense is in reality this unprofessional, and it's likely if not guaranteed that some of the early-season miscommunications that made the Lions defense so terrible have been ironed out. That's probably factored into the betting line, which is fascinating: Detroit is favored by 3.5 points. They're at home, and their offense is as good as it gets, but Vegas does not buy the Packers recent hot streak at all. Give me the Lions.
