picks.headline: Vikings at Lions: Predictions, picks and odds for NFL Week 8 game
picks.blurb: 1. Defense wins championships, but will it win this game? The Lions and Vikings couldn't be more opposite at this point in the season. Minnesota is winning with defense, and Detroit is getting by with an electric offense. So it'll be strength vs. strength and weakness vs. weakness in this key NFC North clash. 2. Not-so smooth sailing: The Vikings are about to enter some rough waters when the calendar flips to November. Minnesota cleaned up with wins over the Saints , Dolphins and Colts in October, but the schedule's difficulty is about to be turned up a notch. The Lions, Bills, Packers and Niners await in the penultimate month of the year for the last undefeated team. We're about to find out if the Vikings are a contender or pretender. 3. Scoring drought: For the first time this season, Jahmyr Gibbs didn't get into the end zone. For someone who has his eyes on LaDainian Tomlinson's record of 31, that drought can't last much longer. Gibbs has nine total touchdowns through six games, but he'll still have to pick up the pace. That watch continues into Week 8. Lions vs Vikings odds, moneyline, over/under Opening lines: Spread: Lions -4.5 Moneyline: Lions -218; Vikings +180 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Lions vs Vikings USA TODAY expert picks Adam Kaufman: Lions 23, Vikings 20 The Vikings keep winning, and their defense keeps making everybody miserable. That travels. But the Lions present a much tougher offensive assignment than the Colts, especially with Jahmyr Gibbs creating problems as both a runner and receiver. Detroit's best approach is keeping Jared Goff out of obvious passing situations, where Brian Flores can turn an ordinary Sunday into an escape room. Minnesota's historically bad offense remains the concern. Can it consistently hold up its end against a team capable of sustaining drives? I'm expecting a tight, physical division game, with the Lions bouncing back to produce just enough offense to hand the Vikings their first loss. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Lions 20, Vikings 13 This might be the end of the line for the Vikings' undefeated run. While Brian Flores' vise-grip defense gives Minnesota a chance in any contest, it will be exceedingly difficult if the Kyler Murray-led offense remains out of sync. Deroit's defense isn't inspiring fear in anyone, but Brian Branch's return has helped the unit at least approach reliability. Jared Goff has the third-highest passer rating of any quarterback against the blitz this year, so Flores might have to be particularly creative in how he tries to box in the Lions' attack. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Lions 21, Vikings 17 Unstoppable force meets immovable object. The Lions defense couldn't catch a cold this season, and the Vikings offense appears to be doing their best to boost Brian Flores' chances of landing a head coaching job this offseason. If you like chaos, this Flores defense is for you. Physical and blitz-heavy, Minnesota is the last unbeaten team solely because of that unit. However, it's hard to have any faith in the Kyler Murray-led unit on the other side of the ball. This figures to be an ugly NFC North contest. Trust the Lions' offense to eke out a win at home. away.headline: Vikings-Lions injury updates: Latest on Aaron Jones, Joe Huber
away.blurb: The Vikings will be without two offensive starters when they practice Wednesday: running back Aaron Jones Sr. (knee) and guard Joe Huber (knee). Jones, who re-aggravated a knee injury he’s been dealing with most of the season Sunday against the Indianapolis Colts , will be day-to-day this week. The Vikings travel to Detroit to take on the Lions this weekend . “He’s doing well,” Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell said. “He feels strong. He feels like he’s gonna be able to progress and get to a good place on game day, but we have to have plans in place regardless.” Jones’ fellow starting running back Jordan Mason (thumb) came off injured reserve last week. The Vikings also roster rookie sixth-round pick Demond Claiborne and have DeeJay Dallas on their practice squad. Huber is dealing with knee soreness, O’Connell said, but the team is “not overly concerned.” Huber has been playing in place of left guard Donovan Jackson, who suffered a meniscus tear against the Dolphins in Week 4. O’Connell said Trevor Keegan and rookie third-round pick Caleb Tiernan, selected as a tackle, will fill Huber’s role at practice for the time being. “Started giving Tiernan some reps inside a few weeks back, and that’s been kind of progressing with ... some splash reps in there at practice,” O’Connell said. ©2026 The Minnesota Star Tribune. away.blurb: The Detroit Lions (4-2) will host the Minnesota Vikings (6-0) in Week 8, and both teams were on the practice field on Wednesday, preparing for their Sunday afternoon battle at Ford Field. The Lions have only a few injured players this week—Amon Ra St. Brown and Ennis Rakestraw were injured in Week 7—but they also elected to rest several injured players on Wednesday; most, if not all, are expected to return to practice this week. “We’re going to do a walkthrough and then roll right into practice for a little bit here,” Lions coach Dan Campbell explained at Wednesday’s press conference. “I think those guys (St. Brown and Rakestraw) will be at walkthrough, but I don’t see them out there during the practice portion. I’m going to hold a couple of other guys back just to get them off their feet, but they’ll be at walkthrough.” RB Isiah Pacheco (MCL/Back, IR) — expected to be out until December “We’re going to start Kerby’s clock today. So, he’ll be running around. Start working him in. He’s put in a lot of work; it’s been a long, hard road for Kerby. So, just being able to get back out there with the guys and run around a little bit. But we will kind of progress him as we go, each week here, just to get him back in the flow, the movement, the flow, the pounding, and all of it. But he’s passed every test to this point, and the next thing is to get him running around now. The strength in the knee is good, and the thigh, the quad, and all of that. So it’ll be great to get him back out there with all the guys.” Joseph has 21 days to be evaluated by the team before they need to decide on his status, but they can return him to the active roster at any time. away.blurb: Though safety Kerby Joseph made his long-awaited practice return on Wednesday, a number of other Lions stars didn't practice for a variety of reasons. Lions head coach Dan Campbell had said earlier in the day that Detroit was planning to hold some players out. "St.'s doing good, Ennis (Rakestraw Jr.) is doing good. Going to hold them out of practice. We're going to do a walkthrough, and then roll right into practice for a little bit here. So, just kinda, it goes all-in-one. I think those guys will be at walkthrough, but I don't see them out there during the practice portion. I'm going to hold a couple of other guys back just to get them off their feet, but they'll be at walkthrough," Campbell said. But, star running back Jahmyr Gibbs also didn't practice and was listed with a shoulder injury. Fellow running back Jacob Saylors (neck) was a limited participant. Like Campbell said, Amon-Ra St. Brown sat out with his ankle injury, and Rakestraw was a limited participant. Starting defensive lineman Tyleik Williams also didn't practice due to illness. Starting right tackle Brian O'Neill was a limited participant with a knee injury. As Campbell suggested, Aidan Hutchinson, DJ Wonnum, Alim McNeill, and Penei Sewell didn't practice as a scheduled rest day. home.headline: Vikings-Lions injury updates: Latest on Aaron Jones, Joe Huber
home.blurb: The Vikings will be without two offensive starters when they practice Wednesday: running back Aaron Jones Sr. (knee) and guard Joe Huber (knee). Jones, who re-aggravated a knee injury he’s been dealing with most of the season Sunday against the Indianapolis Colts , will be day-to-day this week. The Vikings travel to Detroit to take on the Lions this weekend . “He’s doing well,” Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell said. “He feels strong. He feels like he’s gonna be able to progress and get to a good place on game day, but we have to have plans in place regardless.” Jones’ fellow starting running back Jordan Mason (thumb) came off injured reserve last week. The Vikings also roster rookie sixth-round pick Demond Claiborne and have DeeJay Dallas on their practice squad. Huber is dealing with knee soreness, O’Connell said, but the team is “not overly concerned.” Huber has been playing in place of left guard Donovan Jackson, who suffered a meniscus tear against the Dolphins in Week 4. O’Connell said Trevor Keegan and rookie third-round pick Caleb Tiernan, selected as a tackle, will fill Huber’s role at practice for the time being. “Started giving Tiernan some reps inside a few weeks back, and that’s been kind of progressing with ... some splash reps in there at practice,” O’Connell said. ©2026 The Minnesota Star Tribune. home.headline: Lions, Vikings Week 8 injury report: Jahmyr Gibbs sits with shoulder injury
home.blurb: The Detroit Lions (4-2) will host the Minnesota Vikings (6-0) in Week 8, and both teams were on the practice field on Wednesday, preparing for their Sunday afternoon battle at Ford Field. The Lions have only a few injured players this week—Amon Ra St. Brown and Ennis Rakestraw were injured in Week 7—but they also elected to rest several injured players on Wednesday; most, if not all, are expected to return to practice this week. “We’re going to do a walkthrough and then roll right into practice for a little bit here,” Lions coach Dan Campbell explained at Wednesday’s press conference. “I think those guys (St. Brown and Rakestraw) will be at walkthrough, but I don’t see them out there during the practice portion. I’m going to hold a couple of other guys back just to get them off their feet, but they’ll be at walkthrough.” RB Isiah Pacheco (MCL/Back, IR) — expected to be out until December “We’re going to start Kerby’s clock today. So, he’ll be running around. Start working him in. He’s put in a lot of work; it’s been a long, hard road for Kerby. So, just being able to get back out there with the guys and run around a little bit. But we will kind of progress him as we go, each week here, just to get him back in the flow, the movement, the flow, the pounding, and all of it. But he’s passed every test to this point, and the next thing is to get him running around now. The strength in the knee is good, and the thigh, the quad, and all of that. So it’ll be great to get him back out there with all the guys.” Joseph has 21 days to be evaluated by the team before they need to decide on his status, but they can return him to the active roster at any time. While St. Brown was injured in Week 7, his absence from Wednesday’s practice was planned, and he is expected to return to practice on Thursday , as Campbell explained on Monday: As for the other four starters, Campbell also noted that their absences are temporary and they are also expected to return to practice this week. This rest day was designed to “get them off their feet” and allow them an extra day to rest their bodies. Saylors did not appear to suffer an injury during the game, but can often creep in after the game concludes. Fortunately, a limited practice is a good sign. Additionally, the Lions received terrific news on Wednesday, as All-Pro safety Kerby Joseph is now healthy enough to practice, and the team has started his injury evaluation clock , making him eligible to practice. home.headline: Jahmyr Gibbs misses Lions practice with new injury
home.blurb: The Lions had several starters missing from practice as coach Dan Campbell tried to get players "off their feet" ahead of a pivotal division game against the Minnesota Vikings at Ford Field this week. But Gibbs, wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown (ankle) and defensive tackle Tyleik Williams (illness) were all missing for injury- or illness-related reasons. Offensive tackle Penei Sewell and defensive linemen Aidan Hutchinson, Alim McNeill and DJ Wonnum were all absent from the field during the portion of practice accessible to the media, but all had "rest" designations. Any time Gibbs misses would put the Lions into something just shy of crisis mode. The "bell cow" back has accounted for 53% of the team's offensive touches with 166 carries and receptions and 35.9% of the team's scrimmage yards (890) through six games. It's currently unclear how severe the injury is. Gibbs went down awkwardly at the end of the team's 20-17 win over the Green Bay Packers at Ford Field this past Sunday but was cleared of an ankle injury. Gibbs had 29 carries for 116 yards and five catches for 27 yards in the victory. St. Brown was the only player who was truly expected not to be at practice, as he deals with an ankle injury sustained in a 20-17 win over the Green Bay Packers . Two notable players who were present: safety Kerby Joseph and cornerback Ennis Rakestraw. Joseph (knee) practiced for the first time this season, while Rakestraw (ankle) was not expected to practice until Thursday.

home.headline: Detroit Lions Initial Week 8 Injury Report
home.blurb: According to Detroit's Wednesday practice report, Jahmyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown were among seven players who did not participate , while three others were limited. LP = Limited Participation | NP = Did Not Participate One of the most encouraging developments involves Joseph, who was officially designated to return from the Physically Unable to Perform list Wednesday. His limited participation represents a significant step forward, although it does not guarantee he will play against Minnesota. With Brian Branch already back in the lineup, Joseph's eventual return could provide another major boost to Detroit's secondary. As we recently covered , Joseph is eager to return, but the Lions must continue making careful decisions regarding their injured players. picks.blurb: 1. Klint Kubiak vowed there was "no controversy" at quarterback, where Kirk Cousins will remain the starter. While the 38-year-old might have hit a wall last week in trying to navigate the Rams ' relentless blitzes, the NFL's leading passer is hardly the Silver and Black's biggest problem. Kubiak has bemoaned an inert running game that has left Las Vegas needing to sling its way back into games. It could be tricky to get things going against a Jets defense that ranks fifth in defensive EPA per rush. 2. Can New York finally get Garrett Wilson involved early and often in the offensive game plan? One week after he was essentially a non-factor against the Patriots, Wilson was held without a reception or target in the first half against a woefully undermanned Dolphins secondary. Wilson and Glenn both downplayed the wideout's heated confrontation with quarterback Geno Smith, but expect feeding the receiver early and often to be a point of emphasis for Gang Green. 3. How the Raiders' defense handles the Jets' ground game could determine the course of the game. The Silver and Black allowed a season-high 199 rushing yards to the Rams last week, with a vulnerability that has been apparent all season finally reaching critical mass. New York, meanwhile, has seen Braelon Allen eclipse 100 rushing yards in two of the last three games he's handled as Breece Hall's fill-in. Smith threw three touchdowns against Miami, and Las Vegas' defense offers an opportunity for another productive afternoon. The Raiders need more from their running game to keep Cousins from carrying every possession. I'm giving New York the slightest edge at the Meadowlands, and a fifth straight loss for Las Vegas. The Jets' secondary might not be able to mug the Raiders' receiving corps the way that the Patriots and Rams did, but the pass rush should be able to generate sufficient heat to keep Kirk Cousins out of sorts. Las Vegas seems desperate to find any semblance of offensive balance - as well as some stops against the run - but a breakthrough might not materialize this week. It's going to be a bumpy ride to the finish, but there is no doubt the destination is a top pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. That's why it's fitting that New York will get a glimpse at what it could've had last season. Fernando Mendoza won't play, but it's the idea he's wearing silver and black that sticks. away.headline: Las Vegas Raiders Are Betting a Tough Roster Call Will Pay Off in Week 8
away.blurb: Thornton, a 2025 fourth-round pick, had 10 catches for 135 yards as a rookie. His return gives the offense another available receiver, but it also begins a new round of roster decisions. Wide receiver Jack Bech is designated to return from injured reserve. Bech remains on the reserve/injured list after suffering a broken forearm in Week 3, leaving the Raiders to keep balancing short-term availability against their larger depth picture. Laulu’s departure stands out because he supplied meaningful production in 2025, when he was credited with 51 tackles/assisted tackles, eight tackles for loss and four sacks. He had been a healthy scratch twice through seven games this season, however, and the move signals the current staff sees a different need heading into the Jets matchup. Locked On Raiders host Qiant Myers said the decision may reflect the club’s need to get more from its defensive front, particularly after J.J. Pegues forced a fumble against the Los Angeles Rams. Laulu could return via the practice squad if he clears waivers, but the immediate consequence is clear: Thornton has a chance to contribute now, while the Raiders have one fewer proven interior line option. The transaction also puts more pressure on the Raiders to make their game roster count against New York. A Thornton return could help the passing game and create more flexibility for offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak, but the defense will need its remaining tackles to hold up after surrendering 35 points to the Rams. home.headline: New York Jets Add David Bailey, Braelon Allen to Injury Report
home.blurb: The latest addition is star rookie edge rusher David Bailey, who has a groin injury that is keeping him out of practice on Wednesday. Bailey sustained the injury against the Dolphins, but finished the game. Head coach Aaron Glenn said Bailey came to the Jets practice facility on Monday and said his groin injury was still bothering him. Glenn declined to speculate on whether the injury would keep Bailey out of the game against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. "We'll see how he operates," the coach said. "We'll see during the week." Bailey did not practice on Wednesday, with Glenn waiting until later in the week to make an official game status designation. Of greater concern may be the absence of defensive tackle T'Vondre Sweat. The biggest player in the NFL, Sweat sustained a knee injury against the Dolphins and is listed as doubtful. Also doubtful for the Raiders game is edge Joseph Ossai, who has an ankle injury. Both are considered week-to-week on availability. Also nursing an ankle is running back Braelon Allen, who ran for more than 100 yards against the Dolphins. He was listed as limited for Wednesday's practice. The Jets' other star running back, Breece Hall, may return against the Raiders after being a game-time no-go against the Dolphins. He has 357 yards since Hall went down in Week 3, and has performed so well that the Jets are trying to scheme a way to have both backs on the field at the same time. "I think you know that Braelon, we also gave him the ball when Breece was with us and playing," Glenn said. "So, I've said this here numerous times: Both of those guys can carry the load. home.headline: Dolphins’ Caleb Douglas cleared to return from ankle injury against Jets
home.blurb: Douglas suffered the ankle ailment in the Sept. 20 loss to the San Francisco 49ers. He returned to practice this week and has been limited in drills Wednesday and Thursday before Friday’s session. After linebacker Willie Gay Jr. popped up on the Thursday injury report due to illness, Hafley said he’s back in the building Friday and feeling better. Gay participated in practice and is deemed questionable to play. The Dolphins have defensive end Rob Beal Jr., who has been back at practice through his hamstring injury, doubtful. Cornerback Reese Taylor, who has hurt quadriceps, is out. Taylor, at least, was seen participating in team stretch and then running and cutting on the side of practice, but he was still deemed a non-participant in practice. Rookie safety Kyle Louis, as he returned to practice this week, appears to be a Saturday decision on whether he is activated off injured reserve with the knee issue suffered in the opener against the Raiders. Listed as questionable, he is at least in play to return. For the Jets, coach Aaron Glenn told reporters Friday running back Breece Hall will be questionable, which held true at the release of the injury report. Hafley said he expects Hall to play after the standout rusher missed three games and he's preparing as such. New York has linebacker and Miami Hurricanes alum Kiko Mauigoa (quadriceps), offensive lineman Max Mitchell (concussion), edge rusher Joseph Ossai (ankle) ruled out. Questionable, along with Hall, are running back Kene Nwangwu (knee) and offensive lineman Dylan Parham (knee). Before Friday’s practice, Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said Douglas will be good to go after missing three games with an ankle injury. The team’s injury report listed Douglas free of any game status designation after he underwent a full practice session. On Friday, Douglas appeared to be moving well running routes on air and catching passes from quarterback Malik Willis . “He's made a bunch of plays in practice,” said Hafley, who noted Douglas had taken part in individual and team portions of practice before Friday. “I'm excited to see him play. He hadn't played in a while. … It brings us some extra juice.” Without him, the Miami passing offense ranks 31st among 32 teams in the league on the year. The 6-foot-4 target who led the team with 94 receiving yards in the team’s opener against the Las Vegas Raiders could provide a boost to the passing game. Hafley also said running back Jaylen Wright, who has been dealing with a nagging foot injury, will play. This is the second time these two will have matched up this year, with the Browns winning the first time around. However, this game feels like it has more riding on it. The winner of this game will sit alone in first place in the AFC North. It's also a chance for Cleveland to take a two-game advantage in division games, which is a critical playoff tiebreaker. What fireworks can we expect in this game? Here are my three bold predictions. Jared Verse gets on the board Aarong Rogers is the most sacked quarterback in NFL history. He would rather eat the ball and take a sack than put the ball in harm's way by throwing a rushed pass that could be intercepted. We saw a taste of that when the Browns sacked Rogers 5 times when they played earlier this year. I'd imagine that the Steelers will change up their game plan after giving up 8 sacks in the last two games as well as the previously mentioned 5 to Cleveland earlier this year. So it could be a new name that gets his opportunity to sack Rogers. Jared Verse does not have a sack yet this season. His production is undeniably down this year, although he has shown flashes of still being a disruptive player. This feels like an opportune time for him to break through and get his first of the season. KC's back-to-back big days KC Concepcion looked great in the Browns win over the Titans last week. He showed the yards-after-catch ability that we knew he had coming out of college. His quickness is a matchup problem, and now that he is adjusting to the speed of the NFL, we might be seeing that more and more. I am betting that the needle is pointing up for Concepcion after his first career 100-yard receiving game last week. So much so that I believe he will repeat that performance and go for over 100 yards again. This first-round pick has all the ability in the world, and we are watching him come into his own before our eyes. Bust out the brooms The Browns have not swept the season series against the Steelers since 1988. This weekend they will have a chance to break that streak, and I believe that they will. Pittsburgh has been a very middle-of-the-road team this year. Their passing game is pedestrian, and they don't do any one thing especially well. They are ripe for the picking. The thing that gives me the most optimism this week is that I believe that the Browns have the coaching advantage. Todd Monken has this team believing in themselves, and we have seen that reflected in several late-game, one-possession wins this season. When push comes to shove, I think Cleveland is just the more mentally tough team right now. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton No one predicted the Browns (5-2) would be tied for first in the AFC North heading into Week 8 of the NFL season, but here they sit as they prepare to play the Steelers (5-2) in Pittsburgh this Sunday. Cleveland has won five of its last six after beating Tennessee 27-24 last Sunday, while Pittsburgh enters on a three-game winning streak following a 16-10 victory over New Orleans in the NFL’s first regular-season game in Paris. The matchup also comes only a month after Cleveland beat Pittsburgh 27-24 on October 1. Last week, Cleveland again showed an ability to win late in their game against Tennessee. After falling behind 14-0 in the first quarter, the Browns rallied behind Quinshon Judkins , who rushed for 96 yards and two touchdowns, and rookie KC Concepcion , who caught eight passes for 129 yards. Deshaun Watson delivered perhaps his best performance of the season, completing 25 of 36 passes for 308 yards while adding a nine-yard rushing touchdown. After Tennessee tied the game with 58 seconds remaining, Watson immediately answered, hitting Harold Fannin Jr. for 36 yards to help set up Andre Szmyt’s game-winning 32-yard field goal as time expired. It was Watson’s fifth fourth-quarter winning drive of the season. Pittsburgh’s latest win was less dramatic but built around the combination it hopes can carry them to a division title and a playoff berth: Aaron Rodgers , an effective running game and a defense capable of closing out tight games. Rodgers completed 19 of 30 passes for 212 yards and a touchdown against New Orleans, including a four-yard score to Darnell Washington that gave him 540 career touchdown passes and moved him past Peyton Manning into third place in NFL history. Jaylen Warren supplied 101 rushing yards on 18 carries. The Pittsburgh defense held the Saints to just 18 rushing yards and Payton Wilson produced a red-zone interception. The biggest storyline may simply be whether Pittsburgh can reverse what happened in Cleveland four weeks earlier. In that Oct. 1 meeting, the Browns built a 21-7 advantage before Rodgers led a fourth-quarter comeback, eventually tying the game at 24 on his three-yard touchdown pass to Pat Freiermuth and ensuing two-point run. Watson then went 4-for-5 for 46 yards on Cleveland’s final drive, positioning Szmyt for a 56-yard field goal with 10 seconds remaining to give the Browns a 27-24 victory. Watson finished with 268 passing yards, one touchdown and one interception, while Rodgers threw for 299 yards and three touchdowns but was intercepted twice; DK Metcalf added 115 receiving yards and Warren ran for 93. That first meeting established the template for Sunday: division rivals comfortable playing close games led by veteran quarterbacks who have repeatedly delivered late, and a Browns team trying to complete an improbable season sweep against a Steelers club returning home looking to reclaim the upper hand in the AFC North. away.headline: Todd Monken updates Jared Verse injury, other Browns concerns ahead of Week 8
away.blurb: Howard feels like the only real wild-card right now, as he left Sunday’s game early with a head injury and remains in the NFL’s concussion protocol. Both KC Concepcion and Grant Delpit were able to work through the protocol and return the following week this season; both players logged at least a limited practice session by Thursday, though. On a positive note, Mason Graham, Carson Schwesinger, and Delpit were all on the practice field to begin a big week of prep for the Steelers. Harden, Graham, and Delpit all missed snaps against the Titans due to injuries but were able to return to the game to help the team finish its 27-24 win in the fourth quarter. Browns news: 4 ruled out vs. Titans (and 4 questionable), Mason Graham set to return The Cleveland Browns opened their preparation for Pittsburgh on Wednesday with a new player on their pre-practice injury report . The team announced that defensive end Jared Verse will open the week as a nonparticipant as he works through a knee injury he picked up during Sunday’s win over the Tennessee Titans. When asked about Verse potentially missing this week’s big divisional road game against the Steelers, head coach Todd Monken expressed optimism . “I don’t anticipate that,” he said. “Just a little bit of swelling, and we just thought it would be good to just keep him off of it.” The Browns were also without right tackle Tytus Howard (concussion) and center Elgton Jenkins (knee) on Wednesday. Jared Verse's knee injury appears minor as Browns get encouraging news to open Steelers week Considering the laundry list of players on Cleveland’s injury report in recent weeks, Wednesday’s update from Monken was positive. The Browns were actually expected to be without defensive back Myles Harden (hamstring) as well, per the team, but reporters spotted the defensive back warming up on the practice field following Monken’s presser. Jenkins’ absence is likely more veteran maintenance than anything. He played all 70 offensive snaps against the Titans last week, per Pro Football Focus. The Browns have a capable backup in Dawand Jones to play right tackle if Howard needs an extra week to recover. Cleveland hasn’t won a regular-season game at Pittsburgh since 2003, a streak of 22 consecutive losses. Monken told reporters that he hasn’t spoken with the team about ending that drought . The Browns potentially having their healthiest lineup in weeks could certainly help that cause. "It has nothing to do with our team this year,” Monken said. “It's a divisional game. What matters is what we do today, how we practice today and how we prepare today for any opponent. It's bigger because it's a divisional opponent." away.headline: Browns Pro Bowler Lands on Injury Report as Key Contributors Return
away.blurb: Browns Pro Bowler Lands on Injury Report as Key Contributors Return - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Browns Pro Bowler Lands on Injury Report as Key Contributors Return The Cleveland Browns seem to be on the mend when the injury report for Sunday's game against the Tennessee Titans came out. Key contributors are back on the field, but they are still not out of the weeds yet, with one surprising player listed as questionable who can influence the outcome in Nashville. Denzel Ward was listed as questionable with a hand injury on Friday's report. He was limited at practice on Friday, and the defense needs him to be healthy. Ward is having an incredible season locking down the offense's top receiver. Another concerning, questionable designation is Quincy Williams with a neck injury. He has been flying around the field in recent weeks, making big hits and causing fumbles. Williams will be key to rushing Cameron Ward and forcing him to make bad decisions leading to errant throws and turnovers. However, Carson Schwesinger is in the lineup and he is so good that he can make up for Williams' absence should he be out for the game. The defense continues to be hobbled as Grant Delpit is also listed as questionable with a concussion. He left last week's game early with the injury, but has not been ruled for this week. The Browns' stagnant rushing game will get a boost as Dylan Sampson has been upgraded to questionable. He suffered an injury in the first game of the season and has been out since. The defensive line gets a major boost with the return of Mason Graham. His injury in Week 4 looked bad, but he avoided the worst-case scenario and is back in the lineup after missing two games. Michael Hall Jr., Kalia Davis, Out Graham will need to be good, as Michael Hall Jr. continues to remain on the injured list and is out again with an ankle injury. Also on the defensive line, Kalia Davis will not play in the game. The defensive line has caused havoc for other quarterbacks and has shut down the running game. Dillon Gabriel, Teven Jenkins, Out Also out is Dillon Gabriel and Teven Jenkins. Gabriel has practiced and the Browns will have to make a decision on his injury designation soon or risk shutting him down for the season. Jenkins is out, but rookie Austin Barber has stepped up and has played well for the offensive line. If a couple of the questionable players can strap it up on Sunday, then the Browns will receive a major boost to help them improve to an AFC North best 5-2. home.headline: Steelers WR Ben Skowronek returns to practice
home.blurb: Steelers wide receiver and top special teamer Ben Skowronek (calf) was limited in Pittsburgh’s Wednesday practice, the team announced . The practice marked his first participation since Week 5. Joining Skowronek as limited on Wednesday was outside linebacker Alex Highsmith, with a groin injury; Highsmith was limited with the same injury last week but still played versus New Orleans in Week 7. A trio of defensive backs — Brandin Echols (hamstring), Jalen Ramsey (wrist) and Doneiko Slaughter (hamstring) — did not participate Wednesday. Echols missed the Steelers’ game against the Saints, while Ramsey has been playing through his wrist injury despite missing practice reps in recent weeks. Slaughter is a new addition to the report. Elsewhere on the Steelers’ participation report, defensive tackle Cam Heyward, outside linebacker T.J. Watt and tight end Darnell Washington did not participate Wednesday with a rest designation. The Steelers’ Week 8 opponent, the Cleveland Browns, have yet to release their Wednesday practice report at the time of this writing.

Aaron Rodgers led the way for the Steelers in their victory over the Buccaneers as he ended the game with 253 passing yards, two passing touchdowns and an interception while DK Metcalf recorded 93 receiving yards. The Steelers will try to grab another victory Sunday as they face off against the Saints in a tough matchup. New Orleans enters Sunday’s game with a 2-4 record after defeating the New York Giants on the road in Week 6. In their victory over the Giants, Tyler Shough led the way for the Saints as he recorded 176 total yards and four total touchdowns while Kendre Miller added 70 rushing yards. away.blurb: Falcons injury report: RB Brian Robinson, LB Divine Deablo ruled out vs. 49ers Skip to main content Primary nav SCHEDULE Atlanta has several key players who are questionable for Sunday's matchup against the San Francisco 49ers. That includes the Atlanta Falcons and San Francisco 49ers, who each enter Sunday's game with availability questions for key players. Atlanta's injury report has been lengthy all week long, but it includes a few players who could be making a return in Week 7. Most notably are cornerbacks A.J. Terrell Jr. and C.J. Henderson. Their return would bolster a secondary that has been dinged up in recent weeks but was playing well at the start of the season. If Terrell, who has been on injured reserve for the last four games, and Henderson do return, that could afford a bit of flexibility in the secondary, especially with slot cornerback Billy Bowman Jr. ruled out for Sunday due to a hamstring injury he sustained late in Week 6. Bowman is one of four players ruled out against the 49ers. The others are linebacker Divine Deablo, offensive tackle Michael Jerrell and running back Brian Robinson Jr., the latter two of whom first appeared on Wednesday's injury report as limited participants with bicep and hamstring injuries, respectively. Deablo has been the key communicator for Atlanta's defense this season, but the team feels confident that rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels, who is questionable for the game with a neck injury , can step up in that area if needed. The Falcons had three players begin practicing this week after spending time on injured reserve. While those three players—wide receiver Beaux Collins, offensive lineman Cameron Williams and Terrell—are listed as questionable for the game, they would need to be added to Atlanta's active roster by 4 p.m. ET on Saturday to play on Sunday. Terrell — whose 21-day window opened earlier this week — Williams can be elevated back to the active roster at any point during said window. home.blurb: Recently, Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles was asked about the availability of Egbuka, Luke Goedeke, and Antoine Winfield Jr. for Week 8. However, the head coach revealed that all three players remain questionable . "They're all questionable," Bowles said. "We're going to see on Wednesday and Thursday what they do, and I'll have a better answer for you." Egbuka returned to limited practice on Friday ahead of the Panthers matchup, yet he was unable to receive medical clearance in time to play. The latest update leaves Tampa Bay waiting for further clarity on his recovery as the team prepares for its next divisional test. However, Egbuka's recovery from both the concussion and foot injury will ultimately determine whether he can return against Atlanta. Until the Buccaneers provide another update following his upcoming practices, his availability for Week 8 remains uncertain. Meanwhile, quarterback Baker Mayfield returned against Carolina after missing three games with a dislocated thumb. However, the quarterback had to lead the offense without Egbuka, who had emerged as one of the Buccaneers' primary receiving options this season. Egbuka's potential absence would be a significant blow to Tampa Bay's passing attack. away.headline: Jaguars-Colts Wednesday injury report: It is time to unleash Jalen Huskey
away.blurb: Johnson was the only Jaguar who did not practice Wednesday, which is not a great sign coming off a bye week. Johnson injured his ankle in the Week 6 loss to the Houston Texans in London, and the Jaguars very well may be without their best safety once they kick off against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 8. Limited in practice for the Jaguars were four players: linebacker Jalani Tavai (hamstring), wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (hamstring), long snapper Ross Matiscik (shoulder), and defensive tackle Ruke Orhorhoro. JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- There should be one clear reaction to the Jacksonville Jaguars' first injury report of Week 8: it is time for Jalen Huskey. Huskey, the No. 100 pick in April's NFL Draft, has yet to log a snap on defense and has only been active for one game. But the Jaguars should use this week to push Huskey toward some real playing time considering starting safety Antonio Johnson missed Wednesday's practice with an ankle injury. With second-year safety Caleb Ransaw on injured reserve and not looking close to returning anytime soon, the Jaguars' options at safety while Johnson recovers are starting safety Eric Murray, backup safety Kaevon Merriweather, second-year special teamer Rayuan Lane, or Huskey. The Jaguars leaned toward Merriweather getting playing time over Huskey at previous points, but it is time for the Jaguars to unleash their rookie. Merriweather has played 45 NFL games and has been in the NFL since 2023, so naturally he has more experience than Huskey does just a few months into his NFL career. But the Jaguars need to see what they have in their young safety, especially as injuries continue to hit the safety room. Even if the Jaguars start Merriweather over Huskey, they should deploy their third-round defensive back as their No. 3 safety. Simply put, Jacksonville has a young, athletic and talented safety who has been waiting in the wings, and it is time to see what he has. That is not to say Huskey would be the solution to the Jaguars' issues with explosive passes allowed, but he would give the Jaguars a dynamic at the safety position that Lane and Merriweather likely would not. Johnson not playing on Sunday would be a significant blow for the Jaguars' defense considering the impact he has made this season, both in coverage and as a blitzer against the run and rushing the passer. But the Jaguars drafted Huskey for situations like this, and it is time to let him play. With that said, there was some good news for the Jaguars on the injury front. Cornerback Montaric Brown was a full participant after missing time with a hamstring injury that has sidelined him for all but six snaps in the Jaguars' last three games. Brown was struggling at times before his injury, but a healthy Brown would help change the math in the cornerback room and potentially allow the Jaguars to play Jarrian Jones in the slot more than he has played since Brown started missing practice and game reps due to injury. home.headline: Jaguars-Colts Wednesday injury report: It is time to unleash Jalen Huskey
home.blurb: Johnson was the only Jaguar who did not practice Wednesday, which is not a great sign coming off a bye week. Johnson injured his ankle in the Week 6 loss to the Houston Texans in London, and the Jaguars very well may be without their best safety once they kick off against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 8. Limited in practice for the Jaguars were four players: linebacker Jalani Tavai (hamstring), wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (hamstring), long snapper Ross Matiscik (shoulder), and defensive tackle Ruke Orhorhoro. JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- There should be one clear reaction to the Jacksonville Jaguars' first injury report of Week 8: it is time for Jalen Huskey. Huskey, the No. 100 pick in April's NFL Draft, has yet to log a snap on defense and has only been active for one game. But the Jaguars should use this week to push Huskey toward some real playing time considering starting safety Antonio Johnson missed Wednesday's practice with an ankle injury. With second-year safety Caleb Ransaw on injured reserve and not looking close to returning anytime soon, the Jaguars' options at safety while Johnson recovers are starting safety Eric Murray, backup safety Kaevon Merriweather, second-year special teamer Rayuan Lane, or Huskey. The Jaguars leaned toward Merriweather getting playing time over Huskey at previous points, but it is time for the Jaguars to unleash their rookie. Merriweather has played 45 NFL games and has been in the NFL since 2023, so naturally he has more experience than Huskey does just a few months into his NFL career. But the Jaguars need to see what they have in their young safety, especially as injuries continue to hit the safety room. Even if the Jaguars start Merriweather over Huskey, they should deploy their third-round defensive back as their No. 3 safety. Simply put, Jacksonville has a young, athletic and talented safety who has been waiting in the wings, and it is time to see what he has. That is not to say Huskey would be the solution to the Jaguars' issues with explosive passes allowed, but he would give the Jaguars a dynamic at the safety position that Lane and Merriweather likely would not. Johnson not playing on Sunday would be a significant blow for the Jaguars' defense considering the impact he has made this season, both in coverage and as a blitzer against the run and rushing the passer. But the Jaguars drafted Huskey for situations like this, and it is time to let him play. With that said, there was some good news for the Jaguars on the injury front. Cornerback Montaric Brown was a full participant after missing time with a hamstring injury that has sidelined him for all but six snaps in the Jaguars' last three games. Brown was struggling at times before his injury, but a healthy Brown would help change the math in the cornerback room and potentially allow the Jaguars to play Jarrian Jones in the slot more than he has played since Brown started missing practice and game reps due to injury. home.headline: Walker Little Can Answer One of the Jaguars' Biggest Questions, Starting in Week 8
home.blurb: If Little can provide the consistency the Jaguars need in Week 8 and beyond to help set up a run toward another AFC South title, the math on the Jaguars' left tackle spot might change. Little would be entering a contract year in 2027, but the Jaguars could see enough out of him this year to know that they have two different options to be their left tackle of tomorrow instead of just waiting to see if Harrison can become that player. Little has been waiting for a chance like this for most of his career. He has had limited stretches of play where he has been seen as the guy at left tackle, but the Jaguars have no other option but to view him as it for the rest of 2027. JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- Few Jacksonville Jaguars have as much to gain over the next three months as Walker Little. Little is set to step in at left tackle for the rest of the season following the season-ending knee injury sustained by starting left tackle Anton Harrison, giving Little a chance to not just once again prove his worth, but also givng him a chance to answer one of the Jaguars' biggest and most looming questions entering future seasons. Simply put, the future of the Jaguars' left tackle spot is a complete coin toss right now. While there has been hyperfocus about the Jaguars' pass-rush and defensive front in general, it is clear that the Jaguars' biggest 2027 need as of today is left tackle. Harrison was supposed to be the long-term answer at the spot, of course, but his injury has created quite the question mark for whether he has done enough to prove himself as the answer. “Yeah, bummer for Anton and our team, really. I've been very proud of Anton, and he will be sorely missed. I really felt like Anton had been playing really good football, really all in with the group, his buy-in, his attention to detail, the way he'd been playing. I was very proud of Anton and the way he was playing for us," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said about Harrison's injury earlier this week. The Jaguars would have loved to see Harrison establish himself as the left tackle of the future this year, but the injury means we will not get that answer until potentially next season when Harrison is coming off a serious injury. Could Little, once thought to be the Jaguars' left tackle for years to come, now reclaim his spot and ease the Jaguars' minds at the most important position on the line? "We'll miss him without a doubt but was extremely proud of [OL] Walker Little and the way that he played on Sunday against Houston and stepped up in both the run and the pass," Coen said about Little filling in against the Houston Texans. Did some really good things for us and, no flinch, no blink, next man up mentality. Excited about him and his opportunity and there's not many guys that care more than Walker in a lot of ways about this team and about this group of guys. home.headline: Jaguars Get Devastating Injury Update On Left Tackle Anton Harrison
home.blurb: Return Of The 'X-Factor': Brian Branch Makes Lions A Legit Super Bowl Contender my favs Access and manage your favorites here DISMISS Scores National Football League Add FOX Sports on Google Jaguars Get Devastating Injury Update On Left Tackle Anton Harrison Published Oct. 23, 2026 1:01 p.m. ET share facebook x reddit link Jacksonville Jaguars left tackle Anton Harrison will miss the remainder of the season after tearing a ligament in his right knee. Harrison injured his knee during a win against the Philadelphia Eagles at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London on Oct. 11. He spun on the field turf to make a block and twisted his knee when he planted his right leg. Harrison was carted to the locker room. Harrison waited until the Jaguars (4-2) returned from two weeks overseas to have arthroscopic surgery to determine the extent of the damage. The scope Wednesday revealed a torn anterior cruciate ligament. Jacksonville already placed Harrison on injured reserve. Backup Walker Little, who has started 40 games over six seasons with Jacksonville, is expected to replace Harrison in the lineup the rest of the season. Harrison has started 53 games for the Jaguars since they selected him 27th overall in the 2023 NFL Draft. The former Oklahoma Sooners standout moved from right tackle to left tackle this season in hopes of improving Jacksonville’s run game, which ranks 14th this season, up from 20th in 2025. Harrison is Jacksonville's first starter to sustain a season-ending injury in 2026. Reporting by The Associated Press. home.headline: Updating Every Key Jaguars Injury Entering Bye Week: From Anton Harrison to Montaric Brown
home.blurb: Sitting at 4-2 entering Week 7, the Jaguars have a number of injuries that the bye week could aid in terms of getting players back to full speed. So, who is injured and who could return? Jaguars cornerback Montaric Brown has had a 2026 to forget so far. After giving up a few explosive plays during the first two games, Brown sustained a hamstring injury in Week 3 that has since limited him. He missed the Week 4 game due to the injury, played just six snaps in Week 5 the following week, and then did not play last week against the Houston Texans. and part of it has to do with injuries to Brown and others. The fact he hasn’t been put on IR is a good sign, and he might’ve needed the bye week more than anyone else on the roster. His status post-bye will be revealed likely next week. Jaguars’ second-year safety Caleb Ransaw went down with a knee injury in Week 4 and has missed the last two games as a result, which has led to a depth issue at the safety position. It remains to be seen what an actual timetable will look like for Ransaw, with Jaguars head coach Liam Coen giving a “no comment” reply when asked if Ransaw would be out for the season following his injury. Ransaw has missed a ton of time with injuries in his NFL career and has been on IR over the last two weeks. We will likely not know if Ransaw will return until later in the season, but the Jaguars have some legit safety depth issues behind him. The Jaguars’ big fish in free agency last season, Patrick Mekari has not played a snap this year due to a back injury that also kept him out of training camp. Coen did note this week, however, that Mekari is the closest person to returning of the multiple players the Jaguars have on IR. Whether that means he plays or just serves as depth remains to be seen, though the latter seems significantly more likely. “Mekari [OL Patrick Mekari] could obviously be somebody from a depth standpoint that can be available for us to be able to help us as we go, for sure. But I wouldn't see anybody else at the moment,” Coen said. The Jaguars’ second-year defensive end has been on injured reserve since sustaining an upper-body injury during the first week of the season. He had a stellar training camp and could help the Jaguars get more pressure on the quarterback once he is back to 100%, with Coen noting that he is the second-closest player ready to return after Mekari. away.headline: Giants Place RB Tyrone Tracy Jr. on IR; Add Former Chargers Runner to Roster
away.blurb: Taking Tracy’s spot on the 53-man roster is running back Greg Desrosiers, whom the Giants signed off the Chargers’ practice squad. Desrosiers, 5-foot-11 and 200 pounds, signed with the Chargers as an undrafted free agent out of Memphis after this year’s draft. Another week, another New York Giants player is heading to injured reserve. Running back Tyrone Tracy Jr., who injured his hamstring in the second quarter of Sunday’s game against the Houston Texans, will be placed on IR this week, general manager Joe Schoen announced ahead of his annual bye-week press briefing. Tracy, the team’s fifth-round draft pick in 2024, has appeared in all seven games this season without making a start. He has 19 rushing attempts for 55 yards and two touchdowns and has caught five of seven targets for 54 yards and a touchdown. He was looking to record his third straight season with 1,000 scrimmage yards, but that goal now appears to be a long shot. Desrosiers had a six-year college career, playing two seasons each for Louisville, Massachusetts and Memphis. He finished with 211 carries for 1,302 yards and 16 touchdowns, and 76 receptions for 612 yards and seven touchdowns as a receiver. This past summer, Desrosiers appeared in all three preseason games for the Chargers, rushing for 166 yards on 23 carries with one touchdown and catching one of two targets for eight yards. away.headline: Chargers considering placing injured safety Derwin James Jr. on IR
away.blurb: EL SEGUNDO — Derwin James Jr., the Chargers’ versatile Pro Bowl safety, might be placed on injured reserve after suffering a setback in his rehabilitation from a nagging hamstring injury that has limited him to three games this season, Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh revealed on Wednesday. If he’s placed on IR, he wouldn’t be eligible to play again until Nov. 29 against the New England Patriots. He would sit out upcoming games against the Rams, the Houston Texans, the Baltimore Ravens and the New York Jets. He has been sidelined for losses to the Seattle Seahawks, Denver Broncos and Kansas City Chiefs . In addition, left guard Kayode Awosika did not practice because of a leg injury that has limited him to two games this season after signing a one-year contract with a salary cap hit of $1.886 million with the Chargers in March. Wide receiver Brenen Thompson (hamstring) also sat out. What’s more, Harbaugh said several players eligible to return from injured reserve are making progress, but they aren’t sound enough to return to the active roster. home.blurb: Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Davante Adams could return to the team sooner than initially feared. Rams head coach Sean McVay told reporters Wednesday that Adams underwent surgery on his hamstring and is expected to return "on the shorter end" of his six-to-10 week estimated timeline. McVay said that estimation was "based on how everything went" with the clean out surgery. Matthew Stafford and Puka Nacua should be enough to keep the aerial attack rolling against those opponents, but the Rams will be far more dangerous when Adams does return. Adams suffered the injury during the Rams' loss to the Arizona Cardinals on Oct. 18 and missed their most recent victory over his former team in the Las Vegas Raiders. The six-time Pro Bowler led the NFL with 14 touchdown catches last season and was off to a solid start this year with 30 catches for 480 yards and four touchdowns in six games. He exploded for 195 yards and two scores against the New York Giants in Week 2 and followed up with 137 yards through the air in Week 3 against the Denver Broncos. ▶️ Full Giants-Rams Recap 05:46 Despite this setback, Adams has been fairly durable throughout his career. He has never played fewer than 12 games in a season since he entered the league as a second-round draft pick in 2014. He has led the league in touchdown catches three different times. home.blurb: Oct 23 (Field Level Media) - Rams receiver Puka Nacua sustained a calf injury in practice Thursday that is not expected to be serious, NFL Network reported. Per the report, his status is "up in the air" for the Rams (2-4) for Sunday's road game against the Las Vegas Raiders (3-3). Los Angeles head coach Sean McVay is expected to speak to reporters on Friday. The Rams will be without fellow wideout Davante Adams, who was placed on injured reserve earlier in the week with a ruptured hamstring. The other members of the receiver room are Konata Mumpfield, Jordan Whittington, Tutu Atwell, CJ Daniels and Alex Bachman. Nacua, 25, has 37 catches for 417 yards and one touchdown to go with one rushing score in four games this season. He missed two games with a psoas injury. A two-time Pro Bowl selection, Nacua led the NFL with 129 receptions last season and racked up 1,715 receiving yards with 10 touchdowns in 16 games.

home.headline: Myles Garrett injury update, timeline from Rams coach raises eyebrows
home.blurb: Despite growing optimism last week that superstar defensive end Myles Garrett was nearing a return, Rams head coach Sean McVay poured cold water on those expectations Wednesday, announcing that neither Garrett nor tight end Terrance Ferguson will have their 21-day practice windows opened this week. The news comes less than a week after NFL insider Ian Rapoport suggested Garrett could return to practice this week. Those expectations now appear premature. “So whatever reports are out there, make sure they’re accurate,” McVay said. Under NFL rules, players placed on injured reserve must miss at least four games before becoming eligible to return. Garrett satisfied that requirement following the Rams’ Week 5 loss to the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football, but Los Angeles has yet to open his practice window. With McVay ruling out a practice return this week, Garrett’s earliest possible game appearance is now Week 9 against the Washington Commanders in the nation’s capital. “We don’t talk too much about our jobs per se, and our sports. I think that’s like a really fun thing about our relationship,” Kim said. “But the thing about Myles and everyone who knows him is this he is such a hard worker and he is doing everything he can to get back out there. Doing everything he can to get back stronger and he’s well on his way. The thing about that man is he is stubborn in the best ways, and no injury is going to hold him back.” Los Angeles entered the season with Super Bowl aspirations, only to watch injuries steadily strip away important pieces of its roster, as the team got out to a 2-4 start to the season. Garrett was supposed to be a centerpiece of a revamped defense capable of terrorizing opposing quarterbacks. The Los Angeles Rams are going to have to wait a little longer for the cavalry to arrive. That means both players will remain on injured reserve for Sunday’s Week 8 showdown against the Los Angeles Chargers, leaving a Rams team already battered by injuries without two potential reinforcements that could have helped on Sunday. McVay made it clear Wednesday that the Rams aren’t rushing the process, regardless of what reports have been circulating. Garrett has been spotted roaming the sidelines during recent Rams home games, but watching from the sidelines and lining up opposite opposing quarterbacks are two entirely different things. The former NFL Defensive Player of the Year has been sidelined since the Rams returned from their season-opening trip to Australia, when the team placed him on injured reserve following arthroscopic knee surgery. Once that 21-day window begins, the Rams must either activate Garrett to their 53-man roster or leave him on injured reserve for the remainder of the season. There is, however, encouraging news beneath the disappointment. McVay indicated Garrett remains on track in his recovery and continues attacking rehabilitation with the same relentless mentality that made him one of football’s most feared pass rushers.

Not that anyone in Broncos Country needs a reminder. Denver was flogged 31-10 by the Kansas City Chiefs. And the Broncos defense still hasn't tackled Kenneth Walker. Thankfully, and hopefully, Denver gets a crack at a redo this Sunday in Denver. A win at home against Patrick Mahomes, Walker, and Kansas City would give the Broncos the lead in the AFC West. FanDuel Sportsbook has Denver as the home underdog at +1.5 points, though that's basically a pick 'em at this point. The total sits over/under 40.5 points, with a lean toward the over at -115. Win the turnover battle As we saw in the Thursday night win over the Seattle Seahawks, when the Broncos defense creates turnovers and the offense protects the ball, Denver wins. The Broncos have been better at creating takeaways this season, and they need to carry that over on Sunday. away.headline: Chiefs sign former All-Pro Justin Tucker after NFL suspension
away.blurb: Since becoming eligible to return, Tucker has reportedly participated in workouts with several teams, including the New York Jets, Indianapolis Colts, New Orleans Saints and Miami Dolphins. The Kansas City Chiefs are bringing one of the most accomplished kickers in NFL history back into the league following a lengthy absence. Kansas City is signing former Baltimore Ravens kicker Justin Tucker to its practice squad, according to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport and Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star. The move marks Tucker’s first NFL contract since his release from Baltimore in May 2025, which came amid an investigation into allegations of sexual misconduct involving massage therapists. Tucker, 36, spent 13 seasons with the Ravens, establishing himself as one of the most reliable kickers in league history. However, his career took a significant turn in 2025 after 16 massage therapists from eight Baltimore-area spas accused him of inappropriate conduct during massage sessions. The allegations prompted an NFL investigation, which resulted in Tucker receiving a 10-game suspension for violating the league’s personal conduct policy. Tucker has consistently denied the allegations. He was not criminally charged, and the suspension was served while he remained a free agent. Baltimore released Tucker in May 2025, ending a tenure that included seven Pro Bowl selections, five first-team All-Pro honors and a Super Bowl championship. Despite his controversial departure, Tucker’s accomplishments on the field remain significant. He holds the NFL record for the longest successful field goal at 66 yards, which he made against the Detroit Lions in 2021. Tucker also converted 89.1% of his field goal attempts during his time in Baltimore, establishing himself as one of the most accurate kickers in NFL history. His final season with the Ravens, however, was his least productive. Tucker converted just 73.3% of his field goal attempts in 2024, connecting on 22 of 30 kicks. Now, Kansas City is giving the veteran another opportunity as the team evaluates its kicking situation. Current Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker has struggled with consistency, missing 15 total kicks since the beginning of the 2025 season. Tucker’s addition to the practice squad does not guarantee he will replace Butker, but it provides Kansas City with an experienced alternative. The signing represents a significant development in Tucker’s attempt to resume his NFL career, while also bringing renewed attention to the allegations and league discipline that preceded his departure from Baltimore. At that point, the Chiefs must put him on the active roster or place him on injured reserve. KANSAS CITY, Mo. (AP) — The Kansas City Chiefs signed Justin Tucker to their practice squad on Wednesday, giving the five-time All-Pro kicker a second chance in the NFL after serving a 10-game suspension last year for violating the league's personal conduct policy. Tucker spent 13 seasons with the Ravens, earning a reputation as one of the league’s best kickers, before his tenure in Baltimore ended in controversy. The Baltimore Banner reported in 2025 that he had been accused of sexual misconduct by 16 massage therapists at high-end spas, accusations that Tucker called “unequivocally false” and “tabloid fodder.” The Ravens released him that May. And while Tucker was never criminally charged or sued in civil court, the NFL suspended him for the first 10 games of the 2025 season, which Tucker served as a free agent; he became eligible for reinstatement last November. “He's done his suspension, you know? Took care of that business," Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Wednesday, “and I'll leave it at that.” Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker has struggled mightily the past two seasons , missing a pair of kicks in Sunday’s loss in Seattle , and the signing of Tucker provides some competition for him — even though Reid said Butker would kick this Sunday in Denver. “Listen, Harrison, we love. I've told you that before. He's one of my favorite guys," Reid said, “and sometimes things don't go quite the way you want, and you work on that. He understands the business and how it works. We had a practice squad position open. Butker gets it. He knows that's part of the business. He's struggling a little bit and he gets it.” Butker has missed 10 field-goal attempts and five PATs since the start of last season, the most in the league, and they've come at quite a cost. He's the third-highest paid kicker in the league, carrying the sixth-highest base salary on the Kansas City roster. “Obviously he didn't do very good this past game. I'm stating the obvious there," Reid said, "and he's been up and down. This happens. And you know, anybody else in this business, myself included, you have to pick it up and do better. He gets that.” Tucker, who turns 37 next month, hadn't been much better before he was released by Baltimore. He missed 10 kicks during the 2024 season, by far the most during a career that has included seven Pro Bowl selections. home.blurb: The Broncos certainly expected to get more production out of Waddle when they traded the 30th overall pick and the 94th pick in the 2026 draft to the Dolphins while also swapping fourth-round picks next year in order to acquire the speedy sixth-year receiver. But it just hasn't worked out for the team so far, as third-year quarterback Bo Nix continues to go through growing pains while operating under head coach Sean Payton's offense. But now Jaylen Waddle, their top wideout, is in danger of missing their Week 8 divisional matchup against the Chiefs. According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , Waddle aggravated a chest injury on a WR reverse against the Cardinals, putting his status against Kansas City in question. Waddle's status for the game will be determined based on how practice goes this week, according to the report. Waddle dropped the pitch on an attempted reverse, then, when he fell on top of the fumbled ball to recover it, Josh Sweat fell on top of him, aggravating the injury. Broncos offense hasn't been good with Waddle Also read: Stefon Diggs crashes party near top of Week 8 fantasy WR rankings Waddle's production has been anemic so far in 2026. Through 7 games, he has just 26 receptions on 45 targets for 276 yards and 1 TD. If he doesn't miss Sunday's game and plays all 17 this year, he's on track for 63 receptions, 670 yards, and 2 TDs. That's not the type of production you expect when you trade a first-round and third-round pick for a player. His best game so far this year was against the Jaguars when he caught 8 of his 10 targets for 138 yards. But that game was a major outlier. He's had fewer than 5 receptions in five games this year, and his next highest yards total after the Jacksonville game came last week when he caught four passes for 48 yards. Jaylen Waddle's injury update offers cold comfort to a Broncos receiving corp that is underwhelming this year.Icon Sportswire / Getty Images Broncos have few options behind Waddle Despite his lack of production this year, Waddle is by far the most productive wideout the Broncos have on their roster. As a team, the 1,271 passing yards they've accumulated is good enough for 27th in the league. Their seven passing touchdowns have them tied for 24th. A lot of that is the function of the offense. picks.headline: Patriots opponent preview: Are the Dolphins trending up?
picks.blurb: Patriots opponent preview: Are the Dolphins trending up? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Drew Rasmussen starting Game 5 NFL trade deadline proposals WNBA Finals schedule fiasco Anthony Edwards injury impact Week 8 fantasy trade tips Patriots opponent preview: Are the Dolphins trending up? Bernd Buchmasser Wed, October 28, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 9 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Coming off their mini-bye, the New England Patriots return to their division. On Sunday, the team of head coach Mike Vrabel will visit the Dolphins in Miami. The Dolphins are in the middle of a rebuild. They brought in Jeff Hafley and Malik Willis as the head coach-quarterback combo this offseason to replace the departed Mike McDaniel and Tua Tagovailoa, and have invested heavily in rookie talent: no team made more picks in this year's draft than Miami's 13. The organization is building for the future, even though there are some current growing pains. At 1-5 and ranked 30th in scoring differential thus far, the Dolphins have been one of the worst teams in the NFL this season up to that point. That said, they might be trending up. Let's meet them. Dolphins key stats The Dolphins' problems are reflected by their statistics. They are ranked near the bottom of the league in most major categories on both offense and defense. 1-5 (4th AFCE) 4-3 (2nd AFCE) Scoring diff. Points allowed/game Off. yards/game Off. EPA/play -0.122 (29th) Off. EPA/dropback -0.116 (28th) -0.130 (20th) -0.200 (26th) Def. yards/game Def. EPA/play Def. EPA/dropback -0.115 (13th) -0.081 (22nd) Turnover diff. Offensively, the Dolphins have struggled moving the ball both through the air and on the ground. There have been flashes, but the consistency is lacking even though the team has been able to keep turnovers in a comparatively reasonable range (especially when looking to New England's much more talented offense). On defense, a lack of takeaway has plagued the unit, as has an uneven pass rush and an inability to get off the field on third down (52.1%; 31st). The run defense has been a relative bright spot, but considering that opponents are throwing all over the Dolphins — fourth-most attempts (175), highest net yards per attempt (7.5), highest scoring percentage (49.1%) — there simply is no need to run into a veteran D-line on a regular basis. Dolphins 2026 season The Dolphins started their season with five straight losses, including the first three by multiple scores. Since then, however, they have shown some improvement. Their scoring margin of -7 over the last three games is a distinct improvement, as is being able to finally earn a victory last Sunday against the lackluster Jets. Week 1: 27-13 loss at Las Vegas Raiders (0-1) Week 2: 35-13 loss at San Francisco 49ers (0-2) Week 3: 24-10 loss vs. Kansas City Chiefs (0-3) Week 4: 15-10 loss at Minnesota Vikings (0-4) Week 5: 31-24 loss vs. Cincinnati Bengals (0-5) Week 6: Bye Week 7: 28-25 win at New York Jets (1-5) What stands out about Miami's schedule is that it featured the last three unbeaten teams in the league — the 49ers, Chiefs and Vikings — and the toughest strength of schedule among all 32 teams (.667). Granted, the Dolphins being fairly bad played into that, but they have played, and lost to, some very good teams and beaten the worst one they have faced so far. Dolphins active roster Roster up-to-date as of Oct. 28, 5 a.m. ET | *denotes nominal starter Quarterback (2): Malik Willis* (2), Kyle McCord (14) Running back (3): Ollie Gordon II* (0), Jaylen Wright (5 | KR), Kaytron Allen (30) Fullback (1): D.J. Herman (34) Wide receiver (6): Malik Washington* (6 | PR), Chris Bell* (18), Caleb Douglas* (7), Kevin Coleman Jr. (21), Jared Wayne (86), Jalen Tolbert (1) Tight end (4): Greg Dulcich* (85), Will Kacmarek (89), Seydou Traore (83), Justin Joly (80) Offensive tackle (4): Patrick Paul* (52 | LT), Austin Jackson* (73 | RT), Caedan Wallace (77), Chukwuebuka Godrick (79) Interior offensive line (6): Kadyn Proctor* (74 | LG), Aaron Brewer* (55 | C), Jonah Savaiinaea* (71 | RG), Jarrett Kingston (62), Andrew Meyer (60), D.J. Campbell (63) Interior defensive line (4): Zach Sieler* (92), Jordan Phillips* (94), Kenneth Grant (78), Zeek Biggers (93) Defensive edge (5): Joshua Uche* (9), Chop Robinson* (44), Malik Herring (90), Rob Beal Jr. (51), Rodney McGraw (59) Linebacker (5): Jacob Rodriguez* (10), Jordyn Brooks* (20), Willie Gay Jr. (40), Jackson Woodard (42), Shaka Heyward (45) Cornerback (6): Chris Johnson* (3), Jason Marshall Jr.* (4), JuJu Brents* (8), Jaylin Simpson (32), Reese Taylor (35), Marcellas Dial Jr. (24) Safety (5): Michael Taaffe* (16), Dante Trader Jr.* (11), Zayne Anderson (23), Julius Wood (25), Kyle Louis (19) Specialists (2): Bradley Pinion (48 | P/H), LS Tucker Addington (46 | LS) The first thing that stands out about the Dolphins is their commitment to rebuilding from the ground up. As part of that process, they have six rookie starters in their lineup: wide receivers Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas and left guard Kadyn Proctor on offense, plus linebacker Jacob Rodriguez, cornerback Chris Johnson and safety Michael Taaffe on defense. Furthermore, several of their key reserves are first-year players as well, including fullback D.J. Herman, WR4 Kevin Coleman Jr, and their entire three-man backup tight end group. How soon the Dolphins will add a quarterback to the mix will be seen. For now, however, they are riding with free agency signing Malik Willis. Willis has started all six of the team's games since signing a three-year, $67.5 million contract to move from Green Bay to Miami alongside his head coach. In those games, he has completed 87 o f 151 pass attempts (57.6%) for 1,057 yards with four touchdowns and interceptions each. He also has been sacked 16 times and scored three rushing touchdowns. Willis is a hit-or-miss thrower with big-play potential, but overall has been uneven as evidenced by his 31st ranking among quarterbacks in EPA per play (-0.115). Part of the reason might be his supporting cast, which is missing its best player — running back De'Von Achane — and relying on a whole lot of young talent. That said, Willis' top two receivers this year are both veterans: wide receiver Malik Washington (26/289/0) and tight end Greg Dulcich (18/213/0). At running back, meanwhile, Ollie Gordon has stepped up since Achane's season-ending knee injury. He has carried the. ball 72 times for 339 yards and a 4.7-yard average per carry; Gordon also has scored a team-leading four times. Miami's offensive line, meanwhile, is a collection of highly-drafted players. The only non-first- or second-round pick is center Aaron Brewer, a former undrafted free agent who started his career with Mike Vrabel's Titans in 2020. On the other side of the ball, Miami is led by a veteran defensive line. The top players among the group are Zach Sieler and Chop Robinson, who are tied for the team lead with two sacks each. Robinson, meanwhile, has posted a team-high 20 quarterback pressures. Also high on both lists is ex-Patriot and started edge Joshua Uche, who has one quarterback takedown among his 13 pressures. The second level of the defense is led by the aforementioned Jacob Rodriguez, who has impressed since arriving in the second round of this year's draft. His running mate off the ball is first-team All-Pro Jordyn Brooks, who signed a three-year, $48.1 million extension through 2029 this offseason. The Dolphins are banking on Rodriguez and Brooks leading their defense for years to come, and for good reason: both are very good players. The secondary doesn't have the same consistent talent, even though it has received some solid contributions from its youngsters and veterans alike. Safety Michael Taaffe, for example, is leading the team with two interceptions and tied for the team lead with a forced fumble. Overall, however, as illustrated by the EPA per dropback ranking, the Dolphins' pass defense has some ground to make up — and an inconsistent secondary is a big reason for that. Interestingly enough, the Dolphins don't have a kicker on their active roster. Riley Patterson was released after missing three kicks over the first five games, with the team relying on practice squad member Zane Gonzalez since. In his lone game, Gonzalez has not attempted any field goals but gone a perfect 4-for-4 on extra points. Dolphins reserves Practice squad (16): QB Brady Cook (15), RB Carlos Washington Jr. (26), WR A.J. Henning (82), WR Jalen Reagor (88), WR Will Sheppard (81), TE Tre Watson (87), OT Gottlieb Ayedze (72), OL James Easter (65), DT Jordan Jefferson (91), ED Amari Gainer (53), ED Max Llewellyn (57), ED Eric Watts (95), LB Liam Anderson (50), CB Ethan Bonner (27), S Major Burns (43), K Zane Gonzalez (31) IR (6): RB De'Von Achane (28), TE Cole Turner (87), DT Rene Konga (95), LB Ronnie Harrison (56), LB Trey Moore (17) PUP (1): CB Darrell Baker Jr. (22) The most prominent name on the Dolphins' reserve lists is without a doubt De'Von Achane, who will miss the remainder of the season with a torn ACL suffered in Week 3. Coming off a season in which he had 1,838 scrimmage yards and 12 touchdowns, a healthy Achane would be Miami's lead running back and most dangerous offensive player. Dolphins coaching staff Head coach: Jeff Hafley Coordinators: Bobby Slowik (OC), Sean Duggan (DC), Chris Tabor (ST) The Dolphin overhauled their coaching staff this offseason, firing Mike McDaniel and brining in Packers defensive coordinator Jeff Hafley. Patriots might know Hafley from another role, though: he was Boston College's head coach between 2020 and 2023. Hafley brought coordinator Sean Duggan and a significant portion of the defensive staff with him, and also hired Chris Tabor to lead the special teams unit. On offense, there is a bit more continuity: coordinator Bobby Slowik already was with the Dolphins under McDaniel, previously serving as a senior passing game coordinator.

away.headline: Patriots vs. Dolphins Wednesday injury report: Ben Brown returns, while Carlton Davis III ramps up
away.blurb: The starting right guard returned for Wednesday’s practice after missing one week and one game because of a knee injury. Also more than present was starting cornerback Carlton Davis III, who had been limited before being ruled out for a third consecutive matchup due to a neck injury stemming from September.
