home.blurb: Only two players on the active roster missed the first practice ahead of the team's Week 8 game against the New England Patriots, but both rookie guard Kadyn Proctor and cornerback JuJu Brents were out because they're in the concussion protocol. The injury report, though, featured eight players listed as limited participants. The other five players listed as limited were TE Greg Dulcich (ankle), S Michael Taaffe (neck/foot), S Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder), WR Malik Washington (knee) and WR Jared Wayne (knee). Only Trader had an injury reported in the press box Sunday, so it's possible than any of the other four were injured in practice. The most prominent players among those who were limited were wide receiver A.J. Brown (ankle) and starting right tackle Morgan Moses (foot). How the Dolphins' Injury Status Shapes Up Coming Out of the Bye If the Miami Dolphins are going to make it two in a row after getting their first victory of the season, they might have to overcome some injury issues. Because of the fickle nature of concussions, it's impossible to predict whether either or both will be able to play against the Patriots, and Brents was spotted on the outside practice fields at the Baptist Health Training Complex doing conditioning work, which clearly is a good sign. The first injury report of the week for the Dolphins was a long one with 13 names on it, and a new issue for quarterback Malik Willis. After earlier this season being listed with a toe issue and then with a thumb injury, this time Willis is dealing with a groin injury, although he was a full participant in practice Wednesday. Another full participant was edge defender Rob Beal Jr., who has missed the past four games because of a hamstring injury. On the list was cornerback Reese Taylor, who missed the past three games with a quad injury, and long-snapper Tucker Addington and tight end Will Kacmarek both were on the injury report last week before playing in the 28-25 victory against the New York Jets. Head coach Jeff Hafley revealed the concussions before practice before taking questions from the assembled media. Hafley also indicated that backup Jarrett Kingston would be taking Proctor's reps at left guard during practice. Kingston was the one who replaced Jonah Savaiinaea at right guard after the 2025 second-round pick was injured in the first half of the Week 5 loss at Hard Rock Stadium. Kingston, who obviously is the No. 3 guard on the roster, was claimed off waivers from the Houston Texans after the cuts to 53. picks.blurb: 1. Philadelphia needs a reset: The Eagles have dropped five straight after a 2-0 start, with Monday's 38-21 loss to the Cowboys moving them to 2-5. Another division loss would make an already difficult climb even steeper for a team that's more realistically already on to 2027 due to so many key injuries. 2. Keep an eye on Saquon: Speaking of injuries, Saquon Barkley played only nine snaps Monday while dealing with hamstring and back issues. He offered an encouraging assessment of his hamstring and said he doesn't expect the back problem to keep him out. His practice workload still warrants watching. 3. The preparation advantage favors Washington: The Commanders come off their bye, while the Eagles turn around from Monday night for a Sunday road game. That's valuable extra time to prepare for Tanner McKee and the Eagles' reshuffled offense. 4. McKee needs help from his defense: Philadelphia's quarterback threw for 211 yards, one touchdown and one interception against Dallas. The Eagles produced three touchdown drives, but their defense couldn't slow the Cowboys. Sustaining drives only helps so much if the other team keeps answering. 5. We should expect points: With a game total around 40.5, we're not asking for much to hit 41 points, even from these two offenses. The trends are on our side. Commanders coach Dan Quinn is 8-1 to the over in division games since the start of last season, while the Eagles are 7-1 to the over against the Commanders under coach Nick Sirianni. Tanner McKee can keep things functional when the Eagles protect him and stay balanced. That becomes much harder if the Commanders take away the run and force longer passing situations. Washington also has the benefit of a bye and lots of extra rest, while Philadelphia turns around from Monday night. It's so disappointing this is a primetime game. away.headline: Eagles' Saquon Barkley weighs in on potential 18-game NFL season amid injury concerns
away.blurb: In March, ESPN's Stephen Holder reported the NFLPA took a public stance against expanding the schedule to 18 games. However, Holder pointed out it did so before the schedule expanded to 17 games as well before eventually agreeing to a new collective bargaining agreement. Count Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley among those who are against the NFL expanding to 18 regular-season games. "I can't speak on how players feel," Barkley told Dan Roberts of Front Office Sports (9:55 mark). "How do I feel about it? I'm not a fan of it. I actually don't agree with it, to be completely honest. "Yeah, and so if it's up to me and up to my vote on that particular thing that they want to change, I don't think so. … I'm all about players' health. And I don't see how any way adding another game is advantageous to our health for the now and for the future." He highlighted the physical wear and tear of the sport, including at his running back position. "But me personally, if you talk about the best way I can answer it for player safety, I don't see how adding another game is good for player safety," Barkley continued. "And that's just kind of my stance on it. But I know some people agree and a lot of people disagree with it." The comments were particularly notable coming from Barkley, who has dealt with a hamstring injury this season. Mark Maske of Front Office Sports noted the league and team owners are eventually expected to propose expanding the regular-season schedule to 18 games, although any official discussions are on hold while JC Tretter, who is the union's executive director, talks to players on team visits. The NFL expanded to 17 games starting with the 2021 season. If the league wanted to expand the schedule again before the current CBA expires after the 2030 season, it would have to negotiate with the union and surely offer other concessions. For now, it is just something that has been speculated about and discussed, and Barkley was clear where he stood.

away.blurb: The season feels like it's on the line for the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 7 now that Jalen Hurts is out for the season. The ever-forgiving NFC East could keep the Eagles afloat for a bit, but they need to score a win against the Dallas Cowboys on Monday night to keep pace in a wide-open division. The official word on Barkley is expected closer to game time, but all signs are pointing towards the Pro Bowler making his official return in Week 7. The Eagles listed Barkley as questionable but he did practice in full on Saturday, with NFL Network's Ian Rapoport noting that the expectation is for Barkley to take the field on Monday. The fact that this is a Monday night game without a clear call makes life quite difficult for managers with Barkley on their roster. The upside that Barkley offers is enormous, but if he is ruled out prior to the game there are few legitimate alternatives to plug in for him. The good news for Barkley backers is that the Eagles will likely give him everything he can handle if he's active. Both DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks are out for this game, leaving Dallas Goedert and Makai Lemon as the top receiving weapons for backup QB Tanner McKee. It would be a big help if Philly can get running back Saquon Barkley on the field for that pivotal matchup. It would be quite helpful for Nick Sirianni, however, if Barkley can take as much work as possible on Monday. away.blurb: Dallas Goedert is good to go for Monday, while Saquon Barkley and Jalyx Hunt inch closer to a potential return. "It's just kind of the same injury that I sustained earlier. I just had a little bit of inflammation in there, had to let that settle down, but felt really good running out there today," Goedert said after Saturday's practice. "I want to be out there anytime I can. We only get 17 games. To miss a game, to miss two games, it always stinks. So if I can be available, I'm going to do everything I can to play. "I'm going to go out there and do whatever I can to help the team win, whether it's run blocking, pass blocking, or hopefully get a couple catches. We're looking forward to this game playing on Monday night against the division rival. It's going to be a lot of fun. The atmosphere's going to be great and it's a game I wouldn't want to miss." Two of the Eagles' top receivers, DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), have been ruled out, leaving rookie first-round pick Makai Lemon as the primary wide receiver option. "It's definitely a big opportunity with the team," Lemon said. "I'm just super excited to go out there with the guys, put on a good performance. Had a great week of practice with all the guys. So, just trying to go out there and execute. A couple guys are out. So really just, next man up. I got a bunch of trust in the guys next to me, trust in the coaches and the game plan." Smith is joined by defensive back Michael Carter II (abdomen). home.blurb: However, Barkley told reporters that "his hamstring came out great," and added that he doesn't anticipate missing any time with the back injury. The 29-year-old veteran did not return to the game after that, as the rushing burden largely fell on the shoulders of Dameon Pierce from that point forward. "It's kind of the school of thought I come from: I truly love this game, and I feel like if you're able to go, sometimes you've got to push your body to the limit," Barkley said. "I'm trying, it's just not responding the way I want it to respond right now. It sucks because I'm trying to be the best leader I can be, and it's hard when you're not able to be out there and perform for your team." Philly took a 21-20 lead during the third quarter, but it was all Dallas from there, as the Cowboys scored 18 unanswered points to close out the game. Given Barkley's limitations, the absence of wide receivers DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, and the fact that quarterback Jalen Hurts is out for the season, the Tanner McKee-led offense put forth a valiant effort on Monday night. That makes having a healthy and effective Barkley even more paramount, but with the injuries continuing to mount, it is fair to wonder if he will be limited moving forward. Meanwhile, quarterback Caleb Williams has picked up right where he left off since returning from an injury of his own, eviscerating the Atlanta Falcons and the Patriots en route to two straight comfortable wins to improve the Bears' record to 5-2 on the season, and second place in the NFC North behind only the Minnesota Vikings, who remain the last undefeated team in the NFL this year. The running game was a huge part of the Bears' success a year ago, so having Monangai back for Sunday's game against a Seahawks team that just completely shut down the Kansas City Chiefs will be a big boost for Chicago. In any case, kickoff between the Bears and Seahawks is set for Monday evening at 8:15 pm ET from Seattle.
